sentence: Hablo con mi mamá todos los días; ayer hablé con ella por teléfono.
grammar: Hablé presents yesterday's conversation as a completed event. Compare present hablo for the visible daily routine. Regular -ar verbs take -é with yo in the preterite.
note: Por teléfono = by phone. Ella refers to the speaker's mother.

sentence: Ayer comí arroz a las dos de la tarde.
grammar: Comí presents one completed meal at a specified past time. Regular -er verbs take -í with yo in the preterite.

sentence: Yo viví en Puebla de enero a junio; ahora vivo en Toluca.
grammar: Viví presents the former residence as a bounded period. Regular -ir verbs take -í with yo in the preterite. Present vivo gives the current residence.
note: De enero a junio = from January to June; both limits belong to the former residence.

sentence: Ana, ¿tú compraste la camisa ayer?
grammar: Compraste asks about one completed purchase by tú. Regular -ar verbs take -aste in this form; no written accent is needed.
note: Compare present compras with past compraste: the ending distinguishes them.

sentence: Ayer el paquete llegó a la oficina a las ocho.
grammar: Llegó reports one completed arrival. The third-person singular preterite ending -ó carries a written accent; present llega describes the schedule in the earlier card.

sentence: Ayer Luis salió de casa a las siete, antes de la clase de las ocho.
grammar: Salió reports one completed departure. Regular -ir verbs take -ió with a singular third-person subject in the preterite.
note: Antes de = before. Luis's departure precedes the eight o'clock class.

sentence: Ayer Ana y yo trabajamos en la oficina de nueve a doce.
grammar: Trabajamos has the same spelling in the present and preterite. Ayer and the bounded hours make this a completed work session.
note: De nueve a doce = from nine to twelve.

sentence: Ana y Luis, ¿ustedes abrieron la tienda ayer a las ocho?
grammar: Abrieron agrees with ustedes and asks about a completed opening. Regular -ir verbs take -ieron with ustedes or ellos in the preterite.

sentence: Ayer pagué la cuenta en efectivo.
grammar: Pagar changes g to gu before the first-person preterite ending -é: pagué. This spelling preserves the consonant of pagar.
note: Pagar = to pay. La cuenta = the bill; en efectivo = in cash.

sentence: Ayer busqué la llave durante diez minutos; ahora está aquí.
grammar: Buscar changes c to qu before -é: busqué. The preterite presents the ten-minute search as a finished episode.
note: Durante diez minutos = for ten minutes. Qu preserves the consonant of buscar before é.

sentence: Ayer empecé a preparar la comida a las doce.
grammar: Empezar changes z to c before -é: empecé. Empezar a takes an infinitive; this preterite locates the start of the activity.
note: Empezar a = to start doing something. Preparar la comida = to prepare the midday meal; the sentence states its start time.

sentence: El día de mi cumpleaños número diez, jugué al ajedrez con mi papá.
grammar: Jugué uses jug- rather than present jueg-, and adds u before -é. It reports one game occasion on a particular childhood birthday.
note: Cumpleaños = birthday. Mi cumpleaños número diez = my tenth birthday.

sentence: Ayer Ana leyó el mensaje de Luis a las ocho.
grammar: Leer uses y in the third-person singular preterite leyó. Ana's reading is presented as a completed event at eight.
note: El mensaje de Luis identifies Luis as the message's sender.

sentence: Ayer Luis oyó un golpe en la puerta a medianoche.
grammar: Oír forms the third-person singular preterite oyó with y. Here it describes perceiving one discrete sound.
note: Un golpe en la puerta = a knock or bang on the door.

sentence: Ayer el vaso cayó de la mesa al piso a las dos.
grammar: Caer forms the third-person singular preterite cayó with y. The glass is the subject of one completed fall.
note: Caer = to fall. Piso = floor; al piso = onto the floor.

sentence: Yo voy al café todos los días; ayer fui a las diez.
grammar: Fui is the irregular yo preterite of ir. The visible café destination makes its movement meaning clear; voy describes the usual routine.
note: El café is the café as a place. The second clause refers to the same destination.

sentence: La reunión de ayer fue muy corta: solo diez minutos.
grammar: Fue is the third-person singular preterite of ser here. It evaluates a completed meeting; corta supplies the evaluation.
note: Corta = short in duration; muy = very; solo = only. Fue also belongs to ir, but this sentence evaluates an event rather than describing movement.

sentence: Ayer tuve una cita con la médica a las nueve.
grammar: Tuve uses the irregular preterite stem tuv-. It places one appointment in a completed past time frame and has no written accent.
note: Tener una cita = to have an appointment.

sentence: Ayer estuve en casa de Ana de dos a cuatro; ahora estoy en mi casa.
grammar: Estuve uses the irregular preterite stem estuv-. The interval presents the stay as finished; the current location is the speaker's own home.
note: De dos a cuatro = from two to four.

sentence: Ayer hice la limpieza del baño a las diez.
grammar: Hice is the irregular first-person preterite of hacer, with stem hic-. It reports completing a household cleaning task.
note: La limpieza = cleaning. Hacer la limpieza del baño = to clean the bathroom.

sentence: El domingo hizo frío en Puebla.
grammar: Hizo frío describes the weather on a particular past day. The impersonal verb stays singular; this preterite form uses z.
note: Hacer frío = to be cold, describing the weather. The sentence concerns Sunday as a completed day.

sentence: Ayer pude abrir la puerta con la llave; ahora está abierta.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative modal verb
grammar: Pude uses the irregular preterite stem pud-. In this completed episode, pude abrir expresses successful opening rather than general ability.
note: Abierta = open, describing the door's current state.

sentence: Ayer Ana ofreció café y yo no quise tomar.
part_of_speech: negative adverb and first-person singular preterite indicative verb
grammar: No quise presents unwillingness on one particular occasion as a refusal of the visible offer. Quise uses the irregular stem quis-.
note: Ofreció = offered. Tomar means to drink here, with café understood from the offer.

sentence: Ayer, a las nueve, supe la fecha de la reunión por un mensaje de Ana.
grammar: Supe uses the irregular stem sup-. Here it marks acquiring information at a particular moment, rather than already knowing it.
note: Por un mensaje de Ana = through a message from Ana; it identifies how the speaker learned the date.

sentence: Ayer conocí a la maestra de Ana por primera vez, en la reunión.
grammar: Conocí uses regular first-person preterite -í. With por primera vez, it describes becoming acquainted with someone at a completed event.
note: Por primera vez = for the first time. This is the first meeting with Ana's teacher.

sentence: Ayer puse la llave del baño encima de la mesa.
grammar: Puse uses the irregular preterite stem pus-. It reports one completed placement of the identified key.

sentence: Estamos en mi casa; ayer Luis vino aquí a las seis.
grammar: Vino uses the irregular preterite stem vin-. Aquí locates the completed arrival at the speaker's current home.
note: Venir presents movement toward the speaker's location here.

sentence: Ayer yo dije «gracias» a la maestra a las dos.
grammar: Dije uses the irregular preterite stem dij-. It introduces the speaker's exact words at a stated past moment.
note: A la maestra identifies the person addressed.

sentence: Estoy en casa de Ana; ayer traje este libro aquí.
grammar: Traje uses the irregular preterite stem traj-. Aquí gives the destination as the speaker's current location.
note: Este libro identifies the book near the speaker at Ana's home.

sentence: Ayer yo di este lápiz a Ana en la clase.
grammar: Di is the first-person preterite of dar. It is written without an accent. Este lápiz is the transferred item, and a Ana names its recipient.

sentence: Ayer yo vi a la médica de mi mamá en el café.
grammar: Vi is the first-person preterite of ver and has no written accent. Personal a precedes the identified person seen.
note: El café means the café as a place.

sentence: El sábado, durante mi visita a Puebla, anduve por el centro de diez a doce.
grammar: Anduve uses the irregular preterite stem anduv-. Here it describes walking around during a finished two-hour interval.
note: Visita = visit; el centro = the city center. Andar por el centro means to walk around the city center here.

sentence: Ayer hubo una reunión en la oficina de nueve a diez.
grammar: Hubo introduces the occurrence of a completed past event. This impersonal use of haber takes a singular form.
note: The stated hours bound the meeting as a completed event.

sentence: Ayer este libro cupo en mi bolsa pequeña.
grammar: Cupo uses the irregular preterite stem cup-. It reports that this particular book fit inside the bag on yesterday's occasion.
note: Caber = to fit in the available space. Bolsa = bag.

sentence: Ayer mi hermana y yo hicimos la cena antes de las ocho.
grammar: Hicimos combines the irregular preterite stem hic- with -imos for a group including the speaker. The dinner preparation was completed before eight.
note: Hacer la cena = to make dinner.

sentence: Ana y Luis, ayer ustedes no estuvieron en la oficina de nueve a doce.
grammar: Estuvieron agrees with ustedes and uses the irregular stem estuv- plus -ieron. Visible no makes the statement one of absence during the bounded interval.
note: The speaker addresses Ana and Luis directly.

sentence: Ayer mi hermana y yo fuimos a Puebla y volvimos a casa a las diez.
grammar: Fuimos is the first-person plural preterite of ir. The destination and return make this a completed group trip.
note: Volvimos a casa = we returned home; both journeys occurred yesterday.

sentence: Ayer Luis pidió ayuda a la médica por un dolor de cabeza.
grammar: Pedir changes e to i in the third-person singular preterite pidió. Ayuda names the requested help; a la médica identifies the person asked.
note: Un dolor de cabeza = a headache. Por introduces the reason for the request here.

sentence: Ayer Ana sirvió la sopa a las dos.
grammar: Servir changes e to i in the third-person singular preterite sirvió. It reports serving a specified food on one occasion.
note: Servir = to serve food or a drink in this context.

sentence: Anoche Luis durmió ocho horas, de diez a seis.
grammar: Dormir changes o to u in the third-person singular preterite durmió. The sentence measures one completed night's sleep.
note: Anoche = last night. De diez a seis spans ten at night to six the following morning.

sentence: Mi abuelo murió en casa el año pasado, con su familia.
grammar: Morir changes o to u in the third-person singular preterite murió. The death is presented as a completed family event.
note: El año pasado = last year. Morir is a direct, neutral word for dying.

sentence: Ayer, a las seis, Ana sintió un dolor en el brazo.
grammar: Sentir changes e to i in sintió. The stated time presents the bodily sensation as a particular past occurrence.
note: Sentir un dolor = to feel a pain.

sentence: Durante el viaje de ayer, Luis siguió la ruta marcada en el mapa.
grammar: Seguir changes e to i in the third-person preterite siguió. Here seguir takes a route as its direct object.
note: La ruta marcada en el mapa = the route marked on the map.

sentence: En la cena de ayer, Ana prefirió sopa en lugar de arroz.
grammar: Preferir changes e to i in prefirió. It presents Ana's selection on one past occasion rather than a general preference.
note: En lugar de = instead of.

sentence: El sábado mis hermanos construyeron una mesa de madera para la cocina.
grammar: Construyeron is the third-person plural preterite of construir. This completed building event uses y before -eron.
note: Construir = to build. De madera = made of wood.

sentence: Al principio de la reunión de ayer, Ana y Luis creyeron esa explicación.
grammar: Creyeron is the third-person plural preterite of creer, with y. The visible noun phrase esa explicación identifies what they believed.
note: Al principio de = at the beginning of; explicación = explanation.

sentence: Ayer Ana repitió su petición una vez porque Luis no oyó bien.
grammar: Repetir changes e to i in repitió. Una vez limits the repetition to one additional saying of the request.
note: Petición = request; una vez = once. Luis did not hear clearly.

sentence: Anoche Luis volvió a casa a las diez.
grammar: Volvió keeps o in the preterite stem volv-, unlike the present form vuelvo. It reports one completed return.
note: Volver a casa = to return home.

sentence: El martes devolví a Ana el libro prestado.
grammar: Devolví keeps the stem devolv- and adds first-person preterite -í. Devolver returns an object to someone; volver describes returning oneself to a place.
note: El libro prestado = the borrowed book. A Ana identifies the person receiving it back.

sentence: Ayer perdí la llave del baño en el camión.
grammar: Perdí uses stem perd- plus first-person preterite -í. The preterite has no e-to-ie change, unlike present pierdo.
note: Perder = to lose. This sentence describes one loss of a particular key.

sentence: Ayer, con el dibujo de la maestra, por fin entendí la instrucción.
grammar: Entendí keeps stem entend- in the preterite, unlike present entiendo. Por fin presents reaching an understanding at that past point.
note: Dibujo = drawing; instrucción = instruction; por fin = finally.

sentence: Ayer busqué mi camisa y la encontré debajo de la cama.
grammar: Encontré uses preterite stem encontr- without the present diphthong of encuentro. It gives the successful outcome of the visible search.
note: Debajo de la cama = under the bed. La refers to the shirt.

sentence: Ayer, a las ocho, recordé mi cita con la médica.
grammar: Recordé uses preterite stem record- without the present diphthong of recuerdo. The speaker directly remembers the appointment.
note: Recordar una cita = to remember an appointment.

sentence: Ayer conseguí una cita con la médica para el lunes.
grammar: Conseguí uses stem consegu- with gu before í, contrasting with present consigo. It reports successfully obtaining the appointment.
note: Conseguir una cita = to obtain an appointment. Para el lunes schedules it for Monday.

sentence: Ayer, en la tienda, escogí una camisa verde y pagué en efectivo.
grammar: Escogí keeps the dictionary stem escog- and adds first-person preterite -í. Its spelling uses g, unlike present escojo.
note: Escoger = to choose. The payment makes this a completed purchase.

sentence: El lunes, a pesar del retraso, Ana y Luis llegaron a Puebla a las diez.
grammar: Llegaron combines llegar with plural -ar preterite ending -aron. It confirms that both travelers reached the destination.
note: A pesar del retraso = despite the delay.

sentence: Ayer Luis intentó abrir la puerta con la llave, pero no pudo abrirla.
part_of_speech: negative adverb and third-person singular preterite indicative modal verb
grammar: No pudo uses irregular stem pud-. After the explicit attempt, it states failure to accomplish the opening on that occasion.
note: Intentó = tried. Abrirla = to open it, referring to the door.

sentence: Ayer Ana quiso ayudar con la cena y dijo: «Yo hago la sopa».
grammar: Quiso uses irregular stem quis-. Ana's quoted offer makes this a particular expression of willingness to help.
note: Dijo = said. Ana offers to make the soup for dinner.

sentence: Ana, ¿cuándo supiste la fecha de la reunión?
grammar: Supiste uses irregular stem sup- with familiar singular ending -iste. Standard preterite supiste has no final s.
note: The question asks when Ana acquired the information.

sentence: Estamos en mi casa; ayer mis padres trajeron pan y leche aquí.
grammar: Trajeron uses irregular stem traj- with plural ending -eron, without i. Aquí identifies the destination as the speaker's current location.
note: The parents brought bread and milk to the home where the speaker is now.

sentence: Últimamente he llamado a mi mamá varias veces.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative auxiliary verb
grammar: He combines with a past participle to form the compound perfect. Here it presents repeated calls over a recent period extending to now; it does not express possession.
note: Últimamente = lately; varias veces = several times; llamado = called.

sentence: Ana, ¿alguna vez has viajado a Puebla?
part_of_speech: second-person singular present indicative auxiliary verb
grammar: Has is the tú auxiliary in has viajado. Alguna vez asks about experience at any time in Ana's life up to now.
note: Alguna vez = ever in this question; viajado = traveled.

sentence: Últimamente Ana ha recibido varios mensajes de su hermana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative auxiliary verb
grammar: Ha agrees with singular subject Ana and combines with recibido. Últimamente frames the messages as repeated experience in a recent period reaching now.
note: Recibido = received; varios mensajes = several messages. Su hermana means Ana's sister.

sentence: Mi hermana y yo hemos estudiado juntos todos estos días.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present indicative auxiliary verb
grammar: Hemos agrees with mi hermana y yo. The compound perfect sums up studying together throughout a period extending to the present.
note: Estudiado = studied; todos estos días = throughout these recent days, up to now.

sentence: Ana y Luis, ¿ustedes han tomado alguna vez el camión a Toluca?
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative auxiliary verb
grammar: Han agrees with ustedes. The question asks about the addressees' experience at any time up to now.
register: Plural address to Ana and Luis.
note: Tomado el camión = taken the bus.

sentence: Yo he trabajado en esta escuela todos estos años y sigo aquí.
part_of_speech: regular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Trabajar forms its participle with -ado: trabajado. Visible he supplies the auxiliary; the final clause confirms the work still continues here.
note: Todos estos años = all these years; sigo aquí = I am still here.

sentence: Últimamente he comido fruta en el desayuno casi todos los días.
part_of_speech: regular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Comer forms its participle with -ido: comido. The compound perfect describes repeated eating over the recent period up to now.
note: Casi todos los días = almost every day.

sentence: Hasta ahora he vivido en tres ciudades.
part_of_speech: regular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Vivir forms its participle with -ido: vivido. Hasta ahora frames the number of cities as life experience accumulated up to the present.
note: Hasta ahora = up to now; ciudades = cities.

sentence: Últimamente he hecho la limpieza del baño cada sábado.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Hecho is the irregular participle of hacer. After he, it describes repeated completion of the cleaning task over the recent period reaching now.
note: Hacer la limpieza del baño = to clean the bathroom.

sentence: Ana, ¿alguna vez has visto una película mexicana?
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Visto is the irregular participle of ver. Has visto asks about movie-viewing experience at any time in Ana's life up to now.
note: Una película mexicana = a Mexican movie.

sentence: Hasta ahora he escrito tres mensajes a mi hermana; todavía no contesta.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Escrito is the irregular participle of escribir. The three messages accumulate up to now, and the missing reply keeps the correspondence currently relevant.
note: Todavía no contesta = she has not replied yet.

sentence: Últimamente he puesto los libros en esta mesa después de cada clase.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Puesto is the irregular participle of poner. Después de cada clase makes the placements repeated across the recent period up to now.
note: Después de cada clase = after each class.

sentence: Últimamente he abierto la ventana todas las mañanas.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Abierto is the irregular participle of abrir. Following he, it expresses repeated opening actions rather than describing the window's state.
note: Todas las mañanas = every morning. The recent morning openings form a pattern continuing up to now.

sentence: Maestra, hasta ahora he dicho tres veces: «Necesito ayuda con la tarea».
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Dicho is the irregular participle of decir. Hasta ahora and tres veces count repeated statements that remain relevant to the current request for help.
register: Direct, insistent address to a female teacher.
note: The quoted words state the help needed with the homework.

sentence: Hasta ahora he vuelto a Puebla varias veces para visitar a mi hermana.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Vuelto is the irregular participle of volver. The destination a Puebla gives volver its return-to-a-place meaning.
note: The speaker counts return visits made in their life up to now.

sentence: Hasta ahora he roto tres vasos en esta cocina; necesito otros.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Roto is the irregular participle of romper. Following he, it reports accumulated breaking events; it is not an adjective describing the glasses.
note: Otros = other ones, referring to replacement glasses.

sentence: Últimamente han muerto varias plantas de mi casa.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Muerto is the irregular participle of morir. Han agrees with plural plantas, while the participle remains muerto.
note: Plantas = plants. Últimamente groups the losses within a recent period extending to now.

sentence: Mi hermana y yo hemos resuelto tres problemas de la tarea hasta ahora.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Resuelto is the irregular participle of resolver. Hemos resuelto counts completed solutions within the work done up to now.
note: Resolver un problema = to solve a problem.

sentence: Mi hermana y yo hemos cubierto la renta de la casa todos estos meses.
part_of_speech: irregular past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Cubierto is the irregular participle of cubrir. With a household expense, cubrir means to meet or pay that cost.
note: La renta = the rent; todos estos meses = all these months, including the period up to now.

sentence: Hasta ahora he leído dos libros de esta autora; quiero leer otro.
part_of_speech: past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Leer forms the participle leído with a written accent on í marking the e-í hiatus. He leído sums up reading experience through now.
note: Autora = female author. Otro refers to another book by her.

sentence: Últimamente he oído golpes en la puerta varias noches y no puedo dormir.
part_of_speech: past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Oído requires an accent on í. He oído describes repeated hearing over a recent period extending to now.
note: Golpes en la puerta = knocks or bangs on the door; varias noches = several nights.

sentence: Últimamente Ana ha traído pan aquí a casa cada sábado.
part_of_speech: past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Traído requires an accent on í. After ha, it describes repeated bringing toward the speaker's home over the recent period up to now.
note: Aquí a casa identifies the destination as the speaker's home here.

sentence: Últimamente esta botella ha caído de la mesa al piso varias veces.
part_of_speech: past participle in a compound perfect
grammar: Caído requires an accent on í. The bottle is the subject of repeated falls; no affected-person pronoun is used.
note: The falls repeat over a recent period extending to now.

sentence: Últimamente he hecho varios favores a mi hermana; todavía necesita ayuda.
part_of_speech: first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: In hacer favores a alguien, hacer means to do favors for someone. He hecho presents repeated favors over a recent period reaching now; a mi hermana identifies the beneficiary.
note: Hacer un favor a alguien = to do someone a favor. The sister still needs help.

sentence: Ana, ¿alguna vez has ido a Toluca?
part_of_speech: second-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Has ido combines the tú auxiliary with ido, the participle of ir. Alguna vez asks about experience at any time in Ana's life up to now.
note: In this experience question, has ido a Toluca asks whether Ana has ever been to Toluca.

sentence: Últimamente mi hija ha tenido problemas con la tarea varias veces.
part_of_speech: third-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Ha tenido agrees with singular mi hija. The difficulty has recurred several times during a recent period extending to now.
note: Tener problemas con la tarea = to have difficulty with the homework.

sentence: Mi hermana y yo hemos estado en la escuela todos estos días para ayudar con las clases.
part_of_speech: first-person plural compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Hemos estado describes the speaker and sister's presence at school throughout the recent days up to now.
note: Para ayudar con las clases = to help with the classes.

sentence: Últimamente mis padres han podido venir a mi casa varias veces.
part_of_speech: third-person plural compound perfect indicative modal verb
grammar: Han podido takes the infinitive venir. Varias veces presents several successful visits over a recent period reaching now.
note: The parents have actually managed to visit on several occasions.

sentence: Siempre he querido aprender a cocinar y ahora tengo tiempo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Siempre he querido presents a wish that has endured up to now. The desired activity remains visible as aprender a cocinar.
note: Siempre = always; tengo tiempo = I have time.

sentence: Siempre he sabido tu nombre completo, Ana; somos amigos de toda la vida.
part_of_speech: first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Siempre he sabido describes enduring knowledge across a friendship continuing now. It does not identify a single moment of finding out.
note: Nombre completo = full name; amigos de toda la vida = lifelong friends.

sentence: Hasta ahora he conocido a muchas personas en esta escuela.
part_of_speech: first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: He conocido counts experience of meeting people up to now. It describes encounters rather than simply stating a current acquaintance.
note: Personas = people. Personal a introduces the people met.

sentence: Nuestro proyecto continúa y mis hermanos han puesto dinero varias veces.
part_of_speech: third-person plural compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Han puesto dinero describes repeated financial contributions. Continúa makes the shared project still ongoing.
note: Poner dinero = to contribute money; proyecto = project; continúa = continues.

sentence: Últimamente mi hermana ha salido con sus amigas casi todos los sábados.
part_of_speech: third-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Ha salido describes repeated social outings over the recent period up to now. Casi todos los sábados supplies the frequency.
note: Salir con sus amigas here means going out socially with her female friends.

sentence: Últimamente mi mamá ha venido aquí a casa todos los domingos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Ha venido describes repeated visits toward the speaker's home over the recent period reaching now.
note: Aquí a casa makes the direction toward the speaker explicit.

sentence: Hasta ahora he perdido tres llaves de esta casa; necesito otra.
part_of_speech: first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: He perdido counts several losses accumulated up to now. The present need for another key connects those losses to the current situation.
note: Otra means another key, referring back to llaves.

sentence: He seguido las instrucciones de la médica todos estos días y ahora estoy bien.
part_of_speech: first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: He seguido describes adherence to instructions throughout the recent days up to now. The participle seguido retains e.
note: Seguir las instrucciones = to follow the instructions. The speaker now feels well.

sentence: Ana, ¿has recibido varios correos de tu hermana últimamente?
part_of_speech: second-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Has recibido addresses Ana with tú agreement. Varios correos and últimamente ask about repeated correspondence during a recent period reaching now.
note: Correos = emails; de tu hermana identifies Ana's sister as the sender.

sentence: Mi barrio ha cambiado poco a poco: ahora tiene edificios en lugar de casas pequeñas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Ha cambiado presents gradual development reaching the present. The visible contrast is between small houses and the buildings now there.
note: Barrio = neighborhood; poco a poco = gradually; edificios = buildings; en lugar de = in place of.

sentence: Después de varios días con dolor de garganta, Ana ha mejorado poco a poco y hoy está bien.
part_of_speech: third-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: Ha mejorado presents gradual improvement leading to Ana's current wellbeing after several difficult days.
note: Dolor de garganta = sore throat; poco a poco = gradually.

sentence: Todavía no he terminado la tarea; necesito diez minutos.
part_of_speech: negative adverb + first-person singular compound perfect indicative verb
grammar: No precedes the complete verb group he terminado. With todavía, it describes a task whose completion is still pending now.
note: The speaker still needs ten minutes to finish the homework.

sentence: De niño, yo hablaba con mi abuela todos los días después de la escuela.
grammar: Hablaba introduces a repeated childhood routine. Regular -ar verbs use -aba with yo in the imperfect.
note: De niño = as a child, for a male speaker; abuela = grandmother.

sentence: De niña, yo comía huevos en el desayuno todos los días; ahora como fruta.
grammar: Comía uses the regular -er imperfect ending -ía for a repeated childhood meal habit, contrasted with the present.
note: De niña = as a child, for a female speaker; como = I eat.

sentence: En esa época, yo vivía cerca de la escuela.
grammar: Vivía gives residence as background at a past time. Regular -ir verbs use -ía with yo in the imperfect; no beginning or ending is asserted here.
note: En esa época = at that time.

sentence: De niño, yo iba a casa de mi abuela todos los domingos.
grammar: Iba is the irregular imperfect of ir with yo. Every-Sunday visits form a childhood routine.
note: A casa de mi abuela = to my grandmother's home.

sentence: De niño, yo era tranquilo; casi nunca hablaba en clase.
grammar: Era is the irregular imperfect of ser with yo. It describes a childhood characteristic as background.
note: Tranquilo = quiet or calm here; casi nunca = almost never.

sentence: De niña, yo veía películas con mi hermana todos los sábados.
grammar: Ver has the irregular imperfect stem ve-: veía. The accent on í is required; the viewing was a repeated childhood activity.
note: Películas = movies; todos los sábados = every Saturday.

sentence: Yo estaba en la cocina cuando Luis salió de casa.
grammar: Estaba gives the speaker's location as background when Luis's completed departure occurred.
note: Cuando = when; salió presents the departure as a completed event.

sentence: Yo tenía ocho años cuando conocí a la maestra de Ana.
grammar: Tenía ocho años states the speaker's age as background when the first meeting occurred. It does not describe acquiring something.
note: Spanish uses tener with a number and años to express age.

sentence: En el patio hacía calor cuando jugué al ajedrez con mi papá.
grammar: Hacía calor supplies weather background during the completed outdoor game. The impersonal verb remains singular.
note: Patio = courtyard or outdoor patio; hacía calor = it was hot.

sentence: De niño, podía caminar una hora sin descansar durante nuestros paseos de cada domingo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect indicative modal verb
grammar: Podía describes general childhood capacity during recurring Sunday walks. It does not report success on one particular occasion.
note: Paseos = walks or strolls; sin descansar = without resting.

sentence: En esa época, yo quería vivir cerca de mis padres, pero mi trabajo estaba en otra ciudad.
grammar: Quería presents an ongoing wish at a past time. It does not describe one refusal or decision.
note: The speaker's job was in a different city from the desired home near their parents.

sentence: Yo ya sabía la dirección de Ana cuando fui a su casa.
grammar: Sabía describes information already possessed when the visit occurred. Compare supe for acquiring information at a particular moment.
note: Ya sabía = already knew; su casa refers to Ana's home.

sentence: Yo ya conocía a la médica de mi mamá cuando la vi en el café.
grammar: Conocía expresses an acquaintance that already existed when the café encounter occurred. Compare conocí for a first meeting.
note: La refers to the female doctor; el café means the café as a place.

sentence: Antes, mi hermana y yo trabajábamos en la oficina todos los sábados.
grammar: Trabajábamos uses first-person plural imperfect -ábamos, including its required accent. The work schedule recurred in the past.
note: Antes here means formerly; todos los sábados = every Saturday.

sentence: De niños, mis hermanos jugaban al ajedrez todas las tardes.
grammar: Jugaban uses plural imperfect -aban and keeps jug-. The present-tense change seen in juego does not occur here.
note: De niños = when they were children; todas las tardes = every afternoon.

sentence: De niña, leía cuentos antes de dormir cada noche.
grammar: Leía retains the stem le- and adds imperfect -ía, with the required accent on í. The reading was habitual.
note: Cuentos = stories; antes de dormir = before going to sleep.

sentence: En esa época, yo salía de casa a las seis todos los lunes.
grammar: Salía presents a recurring departure schedule in the past. It uses sal- plus imperfect -ía rather than present salgo.
note: Todos los lunes = every Monday.

sentence: Cuando yo vivía en Puebla, mi papá venía a mi casa todos los domingos.
grammar: Venía describes repeated visits toward the speaker's home at that past time. It keeps ven- rather than present vien-.
note: The speaker's former home in Puebla anchors the direction of venir.

sentence: Ayer llovía cuando Luis salió de casa.
grammar: Llovía presents rain already in progress as background when Luis left. It does not summarize a whole bounded spell of rain.
note: Llover = to rain. The weather verb is impersonal and singular.

sentence: Anoche yo dormía cuando sonó el teléfono.
grammar: Dormía presents sleep already in progress when the phone rang. The imperfect retains dorm- and uses -ía.
note: Sonó el teléfono = the phone rang, a completed event within the sleeping background.

sentence: Cuando Ana llegó a casa, había dos vasos en la mesa.
grammar: Había gives background existence when Ana arrived. Impersonal haber stays singular even before plural dos vasos.
note: Llegó = arrived; the arrival is the completed event.

sentence: Cuando yo era niño, mi perro se llamaba Coco.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect indicative verb in a pronominal naming construction
grammar: Llamaba supplies the imperfect in se llamaba. The dog's name is background within the speaker's childhood.
note: Mi perro = my dog; se llamaba Coco = was named Coco.

sentence: De niño, llevaba una camisa blanca a la escuela todos los días.
grammar: Llevaba describes customary clothing in childhood. Here llevar means wear.
note: Blanca = white, agreeing with feminine camisa.

sentence: Antes, el pan de esta tienda costaba cinco pesos; ahora cuesta diez.
grammar: Costaba states the former usual price. It keeps cost- rather than the present stem cuest-.
note: Antes contrasts the former price with the current one.

sentence: De niña, a mí me gustaba la leche caliente; ahora prefiero el agua fría.
grammar: Gustaba agrees with singular leche. A mí me identifies the speaker as the person who formerly liked it.
note: Me gustaba la leche caliente = I used to like hot milk; prefiero = I prefer.

sentence: Antes pensaba que Ana vivía en Puebla; ahora sé que vive en Toluca.
grammar: Pensaba introduces a belief held before the speaker's current knowledge. Pensar que introduces the content of that belief.
note: Vivía = was living; vive = lives. The speaker now knows Ana lives in Toluca.

sentence: Yo necesitaba ayuda con la tarea cuando Ana vino a ayudar.
grammar: Necesitaba presents a need already in progress when Ana came to help.
note: Vino a ayudar = came to help.

sentence: Yo esperaba a Luis en la entrada cuando él llegó a las ocho.
grammar: Esperaba presents waiting already in progress when Luis arrived. Personal a remains before Luis.
note: The sentence gives the arrival time without measuring the whole waiting interval.

sentence: De niño, tenía que lavar los platos después de la comida.
grammar: Tenía que plus an infinitive expresses a customary past responsibility. The required action remains visible as lavar los platos.
note: Después de la comida = after the main midday meal.

sentence: De niños, mi hermano y yo podíamos ver la televisión después de la tarea; esa era la regla en casa.
part_of_speech: first-person plural imperfect indicative modal verb
grammar: Podíamos expresses permission for the speaker and brother under a household rule. The first-person plural ending -íamos requires the accent.
note: Regla = rule; the permission applied after homework.

sentence: Ana y yo queríamos ir a Puebla, pero el camión no salió y al final no fuimos.
grammar: Queríamos presents a shared intention already held before the transport problem changed the outcome. It requires the accent on í.
note: Al final = in the end; the bus did not depart, and the planned trip did not happen.

sentence: Antes, yo pasaba por el parque todos los días para ir a la escuela.
grammar: Pasaba describes a customary former route. Por introduces the place along that route.
note: Parque = park; para ir a la escuela = to get to school.

sentence: De niños, Ana y Luis hacían la tarea juntos todas las tardes.
grammar: Hacían agrees with Ana y Luis and describes repeated childhood activity. It uses hac- plus accented -ían.
note: Hacer la tarea = to do homework.

sentence: Ayer yo iba en camión a la escuela cuando sonó mi teléfono.
grammar: Iba presents a journey already in progress when the phone rang. Ayer and the ringing event identify one particular journey.
note: En camión = by bus; sonó mi teléfono = my phone rang.

sentence: De niños, mi hermana y yo veíamos películas en casa todos los sábados.
grammar: Veíamos retains the irregular imperfect stem ve- and adds first-person plural -íamos. The written accent on í is required.
note: Mi hermana y yo makes the speaker-inclusive group explicit.

sentence: Hoy terminé la mudanza; ya vivo en mi casa nueva.
grammar: Mudanza is feminine: la mudanza.
note: Terminé = I finished; casa nueva = new home. The move was completed today.

sentence: Mi hermana vino ayer; su visita duró una hora.
grammar: Visita names the social event; su identifies it as the sister's visit.
note: Vino = came; duró una hora = lasted one hour.

sentence: Ayer no fui a mi cita con la médica por un retraso del camión.
grammar: Retraso is masculine: un retraso. Por introduces the cause of the missed appointment.
note: Del camión = of the bus; the bus delay prevented attendance.

sentence: Ana, hay un cambio de horario: la clase es a las diez, ya no a las nueve.
grammar: Cambio de horario means a schedule change.
note: Horario = schedule; ya no = no longer. The class is now at ten.

sentence: Mi hermana vino hoy sin avisar; fue una sorpresa muy bonita.
grammar: Sorpresa is feminine and takes bonita here.
note: Sin avisar = without letting anyone know beforehand; the visit was unexpected and welcome.

sentence: Tengo un recuerdo bonito de cuando era niño: mi papá y yo en el patio con un libro.
grammar: Recuerdo is a noun after un; it names something remembered.
note: De cuando era niño = from when I was a child; bonito = pleasant here.

sentence: Mi infancia fue tranquila; vivía con mis padres cerca de la escuela.
grammar: Infancia names the period of childhood and is feminine.
note: Fue tranquila summarizes the childhood as peaceful; vivía supplies residence background.

sentence: Mis vacaciones terminaron ayer; hoy vuelvo al trabajo.
grammar: Vacaciones normally names vacation time in the plural and takes plural terminaron.
note: Terminaron = ended; vuelvo al trabajo = I return to work.

sentence: El viaje a Puebla fue de dos días: salimos el lunes y volvimos el martes.
grammar: Viaje names the trip as a bounded event with departure and return.
note: Salimos = we left; volvimos = we returned; fue de dos días = lasted two days.

sentence: Ayer di un paseo por el parque con mi papá, sin prisa.
grammar: Dar un paseo means to take a leisure walk or outing.
note: Sin prisa = without hurrying; the walk was for leisure.

sentence: Ayer hubo un accidente en la cocina: un plato cayó al piso durante la cena.
grammar: Accidente names an unintended incident and is masculine.
note: Piso = floor; durante la cena = during dinner.

sentence: Ayer hubo una avería en el elevador; Ana y yo subimos por las escaleras.
grammar: Avería is feminine and names a fault or breakdown in equipment.
note: Elevador = elevator; escaleras = stairs; subimos = we went up in this past account.

sentence: Ayer trabajé el turno de ocho de la mañana a cuatro de la tarde.
grammar: Turno names a scheduled period of work here.
note: Trabajé = I worked; the shift ran from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon.

sentence: El cumpleaños de mi mamá fue el domingo; comimos juntos en casa.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun with invariant singular and plural form
grammar: Cumpleaños keeps the same written form in singular and plural: el cumpleaños, los cumpleaños. Here el and fue mark one birthday.
note: Comimos = we ate; juntos = together.

sentence: Ayer hubo una celebración en casa por el cumpleaños de mi papá.
grammar: Celebración is a feminine event noun; una introduces one celebration.
note: Por el cumpleaños de mi papá = for my father's birthday.

sentence: Yo estaba en la entrada; Ana me vio desde la ventana.
grammar: Me is the person Ana saw. Yo is the subject of estaba, while Ana is the subject of vio.
note: Me marks the person seen here; in me gusta it instead marks the experiencer.

sentence: Ana, no llamo a Luis; te llamo a ti a las ocho.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar direct-object clitic pronoun
grammar: Te must accompany the tonic personal direct object a ti; the visible contrast selects Ana rather than Luis.
note: A ti emphasizes the familiar listener; ti has no written accent.

sentence: Ana y yo estamos en la entrada; Luis nos ve desde la ventana.
grammar: Nos refers to Ana and the speaker as the people Luis sees. Luis is the subject of ve.
note: Ve = sees; nos includes the speaker.

sentence: Señor Ríos, usted está en la entrada; yo lo veo desde mi ventana.
part_of_speech: masculine singular direct-object clitic pronoun referring to an usted addressee
grammar: Lo refers to Señor Ríos as the person seen. Respectful usted takes third-person forms and masculine singular lo as direct object here.
register: Respectful singular address to Señor Ríos.
note: The speaker addresses the man directly; lo refers to that listener.

sentence: Señora Ruiz, usted está ahí; yo la veo desde mi ventana.
part_of_speech: feminine singular direct-object clitic pronoun referring to an usted addressee
grammar: La refers to Señora Ruiz as the woman seen. Usted identifies the respectful listener; la marks her direct-object role.
register: Respectful singular address to Señora Ruiz.
note: Ahí = there; la refers to the woman being addressed.

sentence: Ana y Luis, ustedes están en el patio; yo los veo desde mi ventana.
part_of_speech: masculine plural direct-object clitic pronoun referring to mixed plural addressees
grammar: Los refers to the mixed group Ana and Luis as the people seen. Ustedes marks those listeners as the subject of están.
register: Neutral plural address to Ana and Luis.
note: A mixed group takes masculine plural los here.

sentence: Ana y Eva, ustedes son mis amigas; las espero en casa esta noche.
part_of_speech: feminine plural direct-object clitic pronoun referring to all-female plural addressees
grammar: Las refers to the two female listeners as the people awaited. Ustedes is the subject of son, while las is the direct object of espero.
register: Familiar conversation with two female friends.
note: Mis amigas = my female friends; esta noche = tonight.

sentence: La clase empieza a las nueve; yo ya lo sé.
grammar: Neuter lo refers to the whole fact that class starts at nine. It does not replace feminine clase alone.
note: Empieza = starts; ya lo sé = I already know that.

sentence: Ana quiere verme hoy en el café; yo tengo tiempo.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Verme combines infinitive ver with attached direct-object me. Ana is the person who wants to see the speaker.
note: Quiere = wants to; tengo tiempo = I have time.

sentence: Luis, tú estás en casa; yo voy a llamarte por teléfono esta noche.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached second-person singular familiar direct-object clitic
grammar: Llamarte combines infinitive llamar with attached direct-object te. Yo is the caller, and familiar addressee Luis is the person called.
note: Por teléfono = by telephone; esta noche = tonight.

sentence: Ana y yo vamos al parque, Luis. ¿Quieres acompañarnos?
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person plural direct-object clitic
grammar: Acompañarnos combines acompañar with direct-object nos, referring to Ana and the speaker.
note: ¿Quieres acompañarnos? invites Luis to join the two people going to the park.

sentence: Señor Ríos, soy el chofer. Puedo esperarlo en la entrada.
meaning: wait for you (one respectfully addressed man)
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached masculine singular direct-object clitic referring to an usted addressee
grammar: Esperarlo combines esperar with lo, referring directly to Señor Ríos as the man being addressed.
note: Lo identifies the male customer being awaited; it does not refer to the driver.

sentence: Señora Ruiz, soy su chofer. Voy a buscarla a su casa a las ocho.
meaning: pick you up (one respectfully addressed woman)
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine singular direct-object clitic referring to an usted addressee
grammar: Buscarla combines buscar with la, referring to the respectfully addressed Señora Ruiz.
note: Buscar a alguien a su casa means to go to that person's home to pick them up here.

sentence: Tus vecinos son Ana y su hermano Diego; quiero conocerlos.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached masculine plural direct-object clitic
grammar: Conocerlos combines conocer with los for the mixed group Ana and Diego. Los replaces a Ana y a Diego; personal a is not retained before the clitic.
note: Quiero conocerlos expresses a wish to meet the two neighbors.

sentence: Tengo prestadas las llaves de Ana; voy a devolverlas mañana.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine plural direct-object clitic
grammar: Devolverlas combines devolver with las, referring to the feminine plural llaves.
note: The keys are borrowed from Ana; devolverlas means giving those keys back.

sentence: Esta mesa es grande; esa también lo es.
grammar: Lo replaces the adjective grande as the complement of es. It remains lo even though mesa is feminine.
note: Esa también lo es = that one is large too. This lo does not replace a masculine object.

sentence: Hoy le doy un libro a Ana.
grammar: Le identifies Ana as the recipient. Un libro is the object given; a Ana makes the recipient explicit.
note: Le can refer to a woman or a man; it does not mark feminine gender.

sentence: Hoy les doy una foto a Ana y a Diego.
grammar: Les marks the two recipients, Ana and Diego. The transferred object una foto is singular.
note: The plural ending belongs to the recipients, not to the number of photos.

sentence: Ana me da un libro; ahora el libro es mío.
grammar: Me marks the speaker as recipient of un libro. Ana gives the book; the book is the direct object.
note: Me is the receiver here, rather than the person seen as in me vio.

sentence: Luis, te doy un regalo: un libro de cocina.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar indirect-object clitic pronoun
grammar: Te marks Luis as recipient of the gift. Un regalo, identified as a cookbook, is the direct object.
note: Te names the receiver here; in te llamo it names the person called.

sentence: Ana y yo no tenemos agua; Luis nos da una botella.
grammar: Nos refers to Ana and the speaker as recipients. Una botella is what Luis gives them.
note: The speaker belongs to the receiving group; Luis is the giver.

sentence: Ella es la maestra; yo le doy el libro a ella.
grammar: The tonic recipient a ella requires accompanying le. Ella is the subject of es in the first clause; yo is the subject of doy.
note: A ella emphasizes who receives the book; it does not replace the required clitic.

sentence: Señoras Ruiz y Mora, ustedes son mis clientas; les doy un recibo.
part_of_speech: plural indirect-object clitic pronoun referring to ustedes addressees
grammar: Les refers to the two women being addressed as ustedes. It is plural because there are two recipients, although un recibo is singular.
note: Les can refer directly to listeners; it does not necessarily mean to third persons.

sentence: —¿Ves a Diego? —Sí, lo veo; le doy una llave.
grammar: Le marks Diego as the recipient of the key. Visible lo marks the same man as the direct object of veo.
register: Familiar singular question and neutral reply.
note: The action determines the role: Diego is seen with lo and receives a key with le.

sentence: Ana recibe un libro de Luis; él le da el libro y yo la saludo.
grammar: La marks Ana as the person greeted by the speaker. Visible le marks her different role as recipient of Luis's book.
note: Saludar takes Ana as its direct object; dar has the book as direct object and Ana as recipient.

sentence: ¿Puedes prestarme tu libro, Ana? Lo devuelvo mañana.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular indirect-object clitic
grammar: Prestarme combines prestar with recipient me. Tu libro remains the direct object of the requested loan.
note: Prestar gives someone temporary use; the speaker explicitly promises to return the book tomorrow.

sentence: Luis, te pregunto algo: ¿a qué hora es la cita?
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar indirect-object clitic pronoun
grammar: Te identifies Luis as the person asked. The following question supplies the information being requested.
note: Preguntar asks a question or seeks information; here the speaker asks for the appointment time.

sentence: Hoy le pido una llave a Ana para entrar.
meaning: her (the person being asked for something)
grammar: Le marks Ana as the person from whom a key is requested. Una llave is the direct object of pido.
note: Pedir una llave requests an item; preguntar seeks information.

sentence: Ana y Diego están en casa; les cuento una historia corta.
grammar: Les marks Ana and Diego as the audience. Una historia corta is what the speaker tells.
note: Contar una historia means to tell a story here, rather than to count.

sentence: Ana y yo vamos a clase; la maestra nos enseña a cocinar arroz.
grammar: Nos marks Ana and the speaker as the people taught. A cocinar arroz identifies the skill being taught.
note: Enseñar a alguien a hacer algo means to teach someone to do something.

sentence: Hoy le mando un mensaje a Ana con la hora de la cita.
grammar: Le marks Ana as the message recipient. Un mensaje is the direct object of mando.
note: A Ana identifies a person receiving the message, rather than a place of movement.

sentence: Mi mamá vive en Puebla; voy a enviarle un paquete a su casa.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached third-person singular indirect-object clitic
grammar: Enviarle combines enviar with recipient le, referring to the speaker's mother. Un paquete remains the direct object.
note: The mother is the recipient; a su casa gives the delivery destination.

sentence: Este libro es mío; Ana me devuelve el libro hoy.
meaning: to me (the owner receiving it back)
grammar: Me marks the speaker as the person receiving their own book back. El libro is the direct object of devuelve.
note: Devuelve describes a return to the owner, rather than a new gift.

sentence: Luis, te ofrezco un vaso de agua.
meaning: to you (the person receiving the offer)
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar indirect-object clitic pronoun
grammar: Te marks Luis as the person receiving the offer. Un vaso de agua is the item offered.
note: Ofrecer presents something for acceptance; the sentence does not say that Luis accepts it.

sentence: El niño tiene un cuchillo; su mamá le quita el cuchillo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular affected-possessor dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Le marks the child as the person from whom the knife is taken. El cuchillo is the removed object.
note: With quitar, this dative identifies the affected holder, rather than someone receiving a gift.

sentence: Ana y yo teníamos una bicicleta; ayer un ladrón nos robó la bicicleta.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affected-possessor dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Nos identifies Ana and the speaker as the owners affected by the theft. La bicicleta is what the thief stole.
note: Teníamos supplies possession background; robó reports the completed theft yesterday.

sentence: Ana tiene su libro, pero le falta un lápiz para la clase.
part_of_speech: third-person singular experiencer dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Le identifies Ana as the person lacking the pencil. Un lápiz is the singular subject of falta.
note: Ana needs the pencil; le does not mean that she is giving something to another person.

sentence: Esta camisa es de mi talla; me queda bien.
part_of_speech: first-person singular wearer dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Me identifies the wearer whose fit is evaluated. The shirt is the understood singular subject of queda.
note: Me queda bien means the shirt fits me well here.

sentence: Luis, ¿te duele la garganta hoy?
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar experiencer dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Te identifies Luis as the person experiencing pain. La garganta is the singular subject of duele.
note: The body part uses la; te identifies whose throat hurts.

sentence: Ana y yo vamos al médico; nos importa la salud de papá.
part_of_speech: first-person plural experiencer dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Nos identifies Ana and the speaker as the people who care. La salud de papá is the singular subject of importa.
note: Importar means to matter or be important to someone here.

sentence: A Ana le interesa aprender a cocinar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular experiencer dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Le identifies Ana as the interested person. Aprender a cocinar is the activity that interests her.
note: The activity takes singular interesa; le refers to the person, not to the activity.

sentence: Puedo leer español, pero me cuesta entender las llamadas.
meaning: for me (the person finding it difficult)
part_of_speech: first-person singular affected-person dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Me identifies the learner who finds understanding phone calls difficult. Entender las llamadas is the task evaluated by cuesta.
note: Costar expresses difficulty here, rather than a monetary price.

sentence: A Ana le parece cómoda la silla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular evaluator dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Le marks Ana as the person making the judgment. La silla is the item judged comfortable.
note: A Ana le parece cómoda presents Ana's opinion about the chair.

sentence: Luis cocina hoy; mañana nos toca cocinar a Ana y a mí.
meaning: to us (the people assigned the turn)
part_of_speech: first-person plural dative clitic pronoun marking an assigned turn
grammar: Nos marks Ana and the speaker as the people whose turn it is to cook. A Ana y a mí makes that group explicit.
note: Tocar plus an infinitive means having an assigned turn here, rather than physically touching.

sentence: A Ana y a Diego les pasó algo bueno: ganaron un viaje.
meaning: to them (the people affected by the event)
part_of_speech: third-person plural affected-person dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Les identifies Ana and Diego as the people to whom something happened. Algo bueno is the singular subject of pasó.
note: The event is explicit: they won a trip. Pasar means happen to someone here.

sentence: Ana salió contenta del examen; le fue bien.
meaning: for her (the person whose outcome is evaluated)
part_of_speech: third-person singular outcome dative clitic pronoun
grammar: Le identifies Ana as the person whose exam went well. Fue in fue bien expresses an outcome rather than movement.
note: Le fue bien means she did well in the stated exam.

sentence: Mi hermana Ana salió de viaje ayer; va a hacerme falta aquí en casa.
part_of_speech: infinitive verbal locution with attached first-person singular experiencer dative clitic
grammar: Ana is the understood subject of va a hacerme falta. Attached me identifies the speaker as the person who will miss her.
note: The speaker will miss Ana's presence at home. Hacer falta expresses missing an absent person here.

sentence: Ana, quiero darte una llave de mi casa.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached second-person singular familiar indirect-object clitic
grammar: Darte combines dar with recipient te, referring to Ana. Una llave de mi casa remains the direct object.
note: The speaker wants to give Ana a house key; te marks the receiver.

sentence: Ana es la maestra; voy a preguntarle por la hora de la clase.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached third-person singular indirect-object clitic
grammar: Preguntarle combines preguntar with indirect-object le, referring to Ana as the person asked. Por la hora de la clase gives the question topic.
note: The speaker seeks information from the teacher; le is the person asked, not the information requested.

sentence: Luis y yo estamos aquí, Ana. ¿Puedes contarnos la historia del viaje?
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person plural indirect-object clitic
grammar: Contarnos combines contar with audience nos, referring to Luis and the speaker. La historia del viaje is what Ana is asked to tell.
note: Ana is the requested storyteller; Luis and the speaker are the audience.

sentence: Yo me lavo las manos con agua y jabón.
grammar: Me refers back to subject yo: the speaker washes their own hands.
note: In Ana me da un libro, Ana acts and the speaker receives something. Here the speaker performs the action on themself.

sentence: Ana, tú te peinas el cabello con un peine.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar reflexive clitic pronoun
grammar: Te refers back to tú, the addressed Ana. She combs her own hair.
note: Te marks self-directed action here, rather than the recipient of something given by the speaker.

sentence: Luis se lava las manos con agua y jabón.
grammar: Se refers back to Luis, who washes his own hands.
note: Luis is both the person washing and the person whose hands are washed.

sentence: Ana y yo nos preparamos para la cita, cada uno en su cuarto.
grammar: Nos refers back to Ana y yo. Each person gets themself ready.
note: Cada uno en su cuarto makes the individual self-directed actions clear; they are not preparing each other.

sentence: Ana y Luis, ¿ustedes se lavan las manos al llegar a casa?
grammar: Se refers back to ustedes, the directly addressed Ana and Luis. Lavan agrees with the plural addressees.
register: Ordinary Mexican plural address with ustedes.
note: The question addresses Ana and Luis themselves; se does not refer to an absent group.

sentence: Tengo jabón y agua; voy a lavarme las manos.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular reflexive clitic
grammar: Lavarme combines lavar with attached reflexive me. The speaker plans to wash their own hands.
note: With las manos, the whole phrase means wash my hands. Me identifies the speaker as the affected person and the actor.

sentence: Cada mañana me levanto de la cama a las seis.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Levantarse means getting up from bed here. Me agrees with the first-person subject.
note: Levantar an object means lift it; levantarse here describes the speaker getting out of bed.

sentence: Me despierto a las siete; todavía estoy en la cama.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Despertarse describes becoming awake. Despierto has the present stem change e to ie.
note: The speaker becomes awake but remains in bed. Waking up and getting out of bed are separate events.

sentence: Por la noche me acuesto en la cama a las diez.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Acostarse means going to bed here. Acuesto has the present stem change o to ue.
note: Going to bed does not by itself say when sleep begins.

sentence: Apago la luz y me duermo en cinco minutos.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Dormirse marks the beginning of sleep. Duermo has the present stem change o to ue.
note: Dormir means sleep; dormirse means fall asleep. En cinco minutos gives the time until sleep begins.

sentence: Por la mañana me baño con agua tibia y jabón.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Bañarse describes washing one's own body. Me refers to the speaker performing the action.
register: Everyday personal-care vocabulary in Mexican Spanish.

sentence: Después del trabajo me ducho con agua tibia bajo la regadera.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Ducharse specifically describes washing oneself using a shower.
note: La regadera makes the shower setting explicit; bañarse is a broader everyday personal-washing expression.

sentence: Cada mañana me visto con una camisa y pantalones para el trabajo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Vestirse means getting oneself dressed. Visto has the present stem change e to i.
note: The shirt and pants identify the clothing the speaker puts on.

sentence: Tengo frío; me pongo mi chamarra.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Ponerse with clothing means putting it on oneself. Pongo is the irregular first-person present form.
note: The speaker becomes the wearer; poner a garment on a table instead describes placing it somewhere.

sentence: Mis zapatos están sucios; me quito los zapatos en la entrada.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Quitarse with clothing means removing it from oneself. Me identifies the speaker as the affected wearer.
note: The shoes belong to the speaker. Compare le quita el cuchillo, where someone takes an item from another person.

sentence: Después de lavar los platos, me seco las manos con una toalla.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Me identifies whose hands are dried and refers back to the speaker doing the drying.
note: Spanish normally uses las manos here: me already identifies the affected person.

sentence: Después del desayuno me cepillo los dientes.
grammar: Cepillo is the first-person present form of cepillar. Me identifies the speaker as brushing their own teeth.
note: Use los dientes here; me identifies whose teeth they are.

sentence: Primero me peino yo; después peino a mi hija.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Peinarse describes combing one's own hair. Peinar a mi hija instead identifies another person receiving the hair care.
note: The visible yo emphasizes that the speaker attends to their own hair first.

sentence: Cada mañana me afeito la cara frente al espejo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Afeitarse describes shaving oneself. La cara identifies the part of the speaker's body being shaved.

sentence: Para la fiesta me maquillo frente al espejo de mi cuarto.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Maquillarse means applying makeup to oneself. The speaker performs and receives the action.

sentence: Yo mismo me corto las uñas con unas tijeras pequeñas.
grammar: Corto is the first-person present form of cortar. Me identifies whose nails are cut; yo mismo explicitly identifies the speaker as doing the cutting.
note: The sentence describes personal nail care performed by the speaker.

sentence: Estoy cansado después del viaje; hoy me cuido y descanso en casa.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Cuidarse means taking care of oneself. The speaker is both the caregiver and the person receiving that care.
note: Resting at home gives a concrete example of the speaker's self-care after the trip.

sentence: Llego a la sala de espera y me siento en una silla.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Sentarse describes moving into a seated position. Siento has the present stem change e to ie.
note: En una silla identifies where the speaker sits down; the verb marks the change of posture.

sentence: Estoy sentado en una silla; me paro y camino a la puerta.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Pararse describes rising to one's feet here. Estoy sentado explicitly establishes the speaker's initial seated posture.
note: Here pararse means stand up; context identifies the intended sense.

sentence: La llave está en el piso; me agacho para recogerla.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Agacharse describes lowering one's body by bending or crouching. The key on the floor explains the movement.
note: Recogerla means pick it up; la refers to the feminine noun llave.

sentence: Tengo una cita a las nueve; me preparo en mi cuarto a las ocho.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative reflexive verb phrase
grammar: Prepararse describes getting oneself ready. Me identifies the speaker as the person being prepared.
note: The appointment provides the reason for getting ready; no object such as food or materials is being prepared.

sentence: Ya terminó la visita; me voy de la casa de Ana.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Irse focuses on leaving. De la casa de Ana identifies the place the speaker departs from.
note: Compare voy a la tienda, which identifies a destination. Here the focus is departure from Ana's home.

sentence: Ana sale de casa; yo me quedo aquí con el niño.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Quedarse describes staying in a place while someone else leaves. Yo explicitly contrasts the speaker with Ana.
note: This is a person's decision to stay, rather than quedar locating a place or describing a quantity remaining.

sentence: Llego a la tienda, pero está cerrada; me regreso a casa.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Regresarse expresses returning or turning back. The closed shop explains the change in the speaker's movements.
note: A casa identifies the destination of the return.

sentence: Estoy lejos de la puerta; me acerco a la puerta para entrar.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Acercarse expresses reducing the distance to something. A la puerta identifies the endpoint approached.
note: The initial distance and the intention to enter make the direction of movement clear.

sentence: La música está muy fuerte; me alejo de la bocina.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Alejarse expresses increasing the distance from something. De la bocina identifies what the speaker moves away from.
note: Here fuerte describes loud sound.

sentence: Son las ocho y mi cita es a las ocho y cuarto; me apresuro para llegar a tiempo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Apresurarse means acting or moving with greater speed. Para llegar a tiempo gives the purpose of the haste.
note: Only fifteen minutes remain before the appointment.

sentence: La cita era a las nueve; me olvidé de la cita y no fui.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase with governed preposition
grammar: Olvidarse takes de before the forgotten thing. Olvidé is the first-person preterite form.
note: The speaker reports forgetting the appointment and consequently not attending it.

sentence: Mi cita es a las nueve; me acuerdo de la hora y salgo a tiempo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase with governed preposition
grammar: Acordarse takes de before what is remembered. Acuerdo has the present stem change o to ue.
note: Acordarse de la hora and recordar la hora express remembering the time, with different complement patterns.

sentence: El examen terminó; me siento tranquilo y contento.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Sentirse followed by adjectives describes the subject's experienced state. Siento has the present stem change e to ie.
note: With tranquilo y contento, me siento means I feel. With en una silla, the same surface form can instead mean I sit down, from sentarse.

sentence: El libro es mío; Ana me lo devuelve hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person singular indirect-object and masculine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Me identifies the speaker receiving the book back; lo replaces el libro. The recipient clitic precedes the direct-object clitic before devuelve.
note: Ana is the actor, the speaker is the recipient, and the book is the returned object.

sentence: Ana, esta llave es para ti; te la doy ahora.
meaning: it to you (the key; familiar singular)
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar indirect-object and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Te identifies Ana as the recipient; la replaces the feminine singular llave. Both clitics precede doy, with the recipient first.
note: The speaker gives the key, and the addressed Ana receives it.

sentence: Luis y yo necesitamos los libros; Ana nos los presta hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person plural indirect-object and masculine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Nos identifies Luis and the speaker as recipients; los replaces the masculine plural libros. The clitics precede presta in recipient-before-object order.
note: Ana lends the books; the speaker belongs to the group receiving the loan.

sentence: Este libro es para Luis; se lo doy ahora.
meaning: it to him (the book to Luis)
part_of_speech: third-person singular indirect-object replacement clitic and masculine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Recipient le changes to se before direct-object lo. Se refers to Luis, and lo refers to the book.
note: This se identifies the recipient; it does not mean that the speaker gives something to themself.

sentence: Ana necesita esta llave; se la doy ahora.
meaning: it to her (the key to Ana)
part_of_speech: third-person singular indirect-object replacement clitic and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Recipient le changes to se before direct-object la. Se refers to Ana; feminine singular la replaces llave.
note: La agrees with the key's grammatical gender. Se identifies the recipient without marking her gender.

sentence: Estos libros son para Ana y Luis; se los doy ahora.
meaning: them to them (the books to Ana and Luis)
part_of_speech: plural indirect-object replacement clitic and masculine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Recipient les becomes se before los. Se represents both Ana and Luis; los replaces the masculine plural libros.
note: Se has the same form for one recipient or several. Los identifies the plural objects.

sentence: Estas llaves son para Rosa y Elena; se las doy ahora.
meaning: them to them (the keys to Rosa and Elena)
part_of_speech: plural indirect-object replacement clitic and feminine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Les becomes se before feminine plural las. Se represents Rosa and Elena together; las replaces llaves.
note: The recipients are plural, but their replacement clitic remains se.

sentence: Esta chamarra es mía; Ana me la devuelve hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person singular indirect-object and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Me identifies the speaker receiving their jacket back. La replaces feminine singular chamarra.
note: Ana returns the item; the speaker owns it and receives it.

sentence: Luis, estos libros son míos; te los presto hasta mañana.
meaning: them to you (the books; familiar singular)
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar indirect-object and masculine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Te identifies Luis as the borrower; los replaces libros. The speaker retains ownership of the books.
note: Prestar describes a loan. Hasta mañana sets its endpoint.

sentence: Luis y yo necesitamos la dirección del médico; Ana nos la manda.
part_of_speech: first-person plural indirect-object and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Nos represents Luis and the speaker as recipients. La replaces the single feminine noun dirección.
note: Several people receive one piece of information; recipient number does not determine the object clitic's number.

sentence: —¿Necesita usted el recibo, señor Ruiz? —Sí, gracias. —Yo se lo doy ahora.
meaning: it to you (the receipt; respectful singular)
part_of_speech: respectful singular addressee indirect-object replacement clitic and masculine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Le for the usted recipient becomes se before lo. Se refers to Mr. Ruiz; lo replaces recibo.
register: Respectful singular address in a service exchange.
note: Yo is the giver. Se represents the addressed customer, so it is not reflexive.

sentence: Ana y Luis, esta llave es para ustedes; se la doy ahora.
meaning: it to you (one key; plural recipients)
part_of_speech: plural addressee indirect-object replacement clitic and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Les for ustedes becomes se before la. La agrees with the single feminine object llave.
note: This sentence follows direct-object agreement: one key gives la, while se represents both recipients.

sentence: Ana tiene mis libros; no me los devuelve hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person singular indirect-object and masculine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: The order is no + me los + devuelve. Me identifies the speaker as the return recipient, and los replaces libros.
note: Negation precedes the entire clitic sequence; the two pronouns stay together.

sentence: Ana, el libro era para ti; te lo di ayer después de clase.
meaning: it to you (the book; familiar singular)
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar indirect-object and masculine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Te lo precedes preterite di. Te identifies Ana as recipient, and lo replaces libro in the completed transfer.
note: Ayer después de clase locates the giving in a completed past event.

sentence: Luis y yo necesitábamos las llaves; Ana nos las dio ayer a las ocho.
part_of_speech: first-person plural indirect-object and feminine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Nos represents Luis and the speaker; las replaces llaves. The sequence precedes preterite dio.
note: The need supplies past background; ayer a las ocho identifies the completed giving event.

sentence: Ana estudia con mis libros; se los he prestado varias veces.
meaning: them to her (the books to Ana)
part_of_speech: singular indirect-object replacement clitic and masculine plural direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Se los precedes auxiliary he in he prestado. Se replaces recipient le for Ana; los replaces libros. Neither clitic attaches to prestado.
note: The perfect summarizes repeated lending through now within Ana's current study arrangement.

sentence: Ana necesita esta llave; yo se la puedo prestar hasta mañana.
meaning: it to her (the key to Ana)
part_of_speech: singular indirect-object replacement clitic and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Se la precedes finite puedo while supplying both complements of infinitive prestar. Se identifies Ana, and la replaces llave.
note: The recipient and object pronouns move together before the modal.

sentence: Este libro es para mí; me lo quiero comprar hoy.
part_of_speech: first-person singular reflexive benefactive dative and masculine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Me identifies the speaker as the beneficiary of their own purchase; lo replaces libro. Both clitics precede quiero while belonging to comprar.
note: The speaker both buys the book and benefits from the purchase. Para mí makes this self-beneficiary explicit.

sentence: Ana, tienes la llave en la mano; ¿te la puedo quitar un momento para abrir la puerta?
meaning: it from you (the key; familiar singular)
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affected-holder dative and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Te identifies Ana as the holder from whom the key would be taken; la replaces llave. The pair precedes puedo while supplying the complements of quitar.
register: Familiar singular permission request to Ana.
note: Ana currently holds the key. Here te identifies the affected source, whereas in te la doy it identifies the receiver.

sentence: Tú tienes mi libro; ¿puedes dármelo hoy?
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached first-person singular indirect-object and masculine singular direct-object clitics
grammar: Dar takes attached me followed by lo. The whole form dármelo carries a written accent to preserve the stress on dar.
note: The listener gives the book; me identifies the speaker receiving it.

sentence: Ana, mi chamarra está limpia; puedo prestártela hasta mañana.
meaning: lend it to you (the jacket; familiar singular)
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached second-person singular familiar indirect-object and feminine singular direct-object clitics
grammar: Prestar takes attached te for Ana and la for chamarra. Prestártela has a written accent preserving the infinitive's stress.
