note: The jacket remains the speaker's possession; the offer is a loan until tomorrow.

sentence: Luis y yo necesitamos los documentos; ¿puedes enviárnoslos por correo?
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached first-person plural indirect-object and masculine plural direct-object clitics
grammar: Nos identifies Luis and the speaker as recipients; los replaces documentos. Both attach to enviar, producing accented enviárnoslos.
note: The listener sends the documents to a group that includes the speaker.

sentence: Este libro es para Luis; voy a dárselo después de clase.
meaning: give it to him (the book to Luis)
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached singular indirect-object replacement clitic and masculine singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Recipient le becomes se before lo even when both attach to dar. Dárselo preserves the infinitive's stress with a written accent.
note: Luis receives the book; the speaker does the giving.

sentence: Ana me prestó estas llaves; voy a devolvérselas hoy.
meaning: return them to her (the keys to Ana)
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached singular indirect-object replacement clitic and feminine plural direct-object clitic
grammar: Se replaces recipient le for Ana; las replaces llaves. Both attach to devolver, with an accent preserving its stress.
note: Ana first lent the keys to the speaker and now receives them back.

sentence: No entiendo este problema; ¿puedes explicármelo con un ejemplo?
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached first-person singular indirect-object and masculine singular direct-object clitics
grammar: Explicar takes me for the person receiving the explanation and lo for problema. Explicármelo needs a written accent.
note: The speaker asks for an explanation using an example.

sentence: Amigo, habla más despacio, por favor; no entiendo tu mensaje.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Habla is the affirmative tú command of hablar. Regular -ar verbs use -a in this command form.
register: Courteous familiar request to a friend.
note: The direct address and por favor establish a request to speak more slowly.

sentence: Hermana, come un poco de sopa; está tibia.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Come is the affirmative tú command of comer. Regular -er verbs use -e for this command.
note: The speaker invites the addressed sister to eat; the sentence does not describe someone's eating habit.

sentence: Hermano, abre la ventana, por favor; hace calor aquí.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Abre is the affirmative tú command of abrir. Regular -ir verbs use -e in this command form.
note: Unlike Ana abre la tienda, this sentence directly asks the listener to open something.

sentence: Amiga, escucha este mensaje de Luis; dice la hora de la cita.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Escucha directs one familiar listener to listen attentively. The message follows as its direct object.
register: Familiar request to a female friend.
note: The message contains the appointment time, giving a concrete purpose for listening.

sentence: Hermana, lee la dirección en este papel antes del viaje.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Lee is the affirmative tú command of leer. It retains both written e vowels.
note: Lee requests reading now or next; leyó reports that someone read in the past.

sentence: Amigo, escribe tu número de teléfono en el mensaje, por favor.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Escribe is the affirmative tú command of escribir. It asks the listener to write the specified detail.
register: Courteous familiar request to a friend.
note: Tu número de teléfono identifies exactly what belongs in the message.

sentence: Hermano, espera cinco minutos en la entrada, por favor.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Espera is the affirmative tú command of esperar. Cinco minutos specifies duration, and en la entrada specifies location.
note: Here esperar means wait, with the requested time and place stated.

sentence: Amiga, mira esta foto de nuestra infancia.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Mira is the affirmative tú command of mirar. It directs the listener's attention to the photograph.
register: Familiar address to a female friend.
note: Mirar takes the thing viewed directly: mira esta foto.

sentence: Hermano, pon los platos en la mesa, por favor.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Pon is the irregular affirmative tú command of poner. The objects are los platos, and their destination is en la mesa.
note: Pon requests an action from the listener; pongo describes what the speaker does.

sentence: Hermana, haz la cena hoy, por favor; yo lavo los platos.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Haz is the irregular affirmative tú command of hacer. Hacer la cena means prepare dinner.
note: The speaker assigns dinner preparation to the sister and dishwashing to themself.

sentence: Amigo, ven aquí a la mesa; tengo tu café.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Ven is the irregular affirmative tú command of venir. Aquí a la mesa marks movement toward the speaker.
register: Familiar invitation to a male friend.
note: The speaker has the friend's coffee at the table and calls him over.

sentence: Hermano, sal del baño, por favor; necesito entrar.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Sal is the irregular affirmative tú command of salir. Del baño identifies the space the listener should leave.
note: The speaker needs to enter the bathroom, explaining the request.

sentence: Amigo, di «gracias» a Ana por la ayuda.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Di is the irregular affirmative tú command of decir. The quoted word gives what to say, and a Ana identifies the person addressed.
register: Familiar reminder to a male friend.
note: Command di means say here. In yo di un lápiz, di instead means I gave, from dar.

sentence: Hermana, ten tu boleto listo; el camión sale a las ocho.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Ten is the irregular affirmative tú command of tener. Ten tu boleto listo asks the listener to have her ticket ready.
note: The upcoming bus departure explains why the ticket needs to be ready.

sentence: Hermano, ve a la cocina; la comida está en la mesa.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Ve is the irregular affirmative tú command of ir. A la cocina identifies the destination.
note: The destination phrase identifies movement with ir; ve here is not a command of ver.

sentence: Amiga, sé paciente; el médico llega a las nueve.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar irregular affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Sé is the irregular affirmative tú command of ser. The adjective paciente describes the attitude requested.
register: Familiar encouragement to a female friend.
note: Command sé has an accent, unlike clitic se. It also differs in function from sé meaning I know.

sentence: Hermano, trae el pan aquí a la mesa, por favor.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Trae is the affirmative tú command of traer. Aquí a la mesa makes the movement endpoint the speaker's location.
note: Unlike Ana trae el documento, this sentence directly requests the listener's action.

sentence: Hermana, da este libro a Luis, por favor; él lo necesita para la clase.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Da is the affirmative tú command of dar. Este libro is the item transferred, and a Luis names the recipient.
note: Da requests giving; di from dar reports I gave. Lo in the second clause refers to the book.

sentence: Amigo, sigue esta calle hasta la farmacia.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Sigue is the affirmative tú command of seguir, with the stem change e to i. Esta calle identifies the route to follow.
register: Familiar directions to a male friend.
note: Hasta la farmacia marks how far along the street the listener should go.

sentence: Hermana, vuelve a casa a las ocho; la cena es a las ocho y media.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar affirmative imperative verb
grammar: Vuelve is the affirmative tú command of volver, with the stem change o to ue. A casa identifies the return destination.
note: The requested return at eight is before dinner at eight thirty.

sentence: Hermano, no hables durante la película; no puedo escuchar el diálogo.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: The negative tú command is no hables, contrasting with affirmative habla. Regular -ar verbs use -es in this negative command.
note: The request concerns speaking during this movie.

sentence: Hermana, no comas ese pan; tiene moho.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No comas is the negative tú command of comer. Regular -er verbs use -as here, contrasting with affirmative come.
note: The bread has mold, making the reason for avoiding it explicit.

sentence: Hermano, no abras esa caja; es el regalo de Ana.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No abras is the negative tú command of abrir. Regular -ir verbs use -as here; the affirmative command is abre.
note: The identified box is Ana's gift.

sentence: Amiga, no escribas tu dirección en el mensaje del grupo; es un dato privado.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No escribas is the negative tú command of escribir, contrasting with affirmative escribe.
register: Familiar practical advice to a friend.
note: The address would appear in a message shared with the group.

sentence: Hermano, no pongas el vaso en esa silla; está rota.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No pongas uses the stem pong- in the negative tú command of poner. The affirmative command is pon.
note: Rota describes the feminine noun silla, so the chair is broken.

sentence: Hermana, no hagas ruido en la cocina; el bebé duerme.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No hagas is the irregular negative tú command of hacer. Hacer ruido means make noise.
note: The sleeping baby explains the request for quiet.

sentence: Amigo, no vengas a mi casa a las ocho; trabajo aquí por teléfono hasta las nueve.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No vengas uses irregular veng- in the negative tú command of venir. Aquí locates the speaker at home.
note: Eight is unsuitable because the speaker works by phone at home until nine.

sentence: Hermana, no salgas de casa sin tus llaves; yo no tengo otra copia.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No salgas uses irregular salg- in the negative tú command of salir. Sin tus llaves specifies what must accompany the departure.
note: The speaker has no spare copy of the key.

sentence: Amigo, no digas «la fiesta es para Ana»; es una sorpresa.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No digas is the irregular negative tú command of decir, contrasting with affirmative di.
note: The quoted words identify exactly what would reveal the surprise.

sentence: Amigo, no tengas el teléfono en la mano durante la clase; necesitas las dos manos para este ejercicio.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No tengas uses irregular teng- in the negative tú command of tener. Tener el teléfono en la mano means hold the phone in one's hand.
note: Holding the phone is a controllable action; the exercise requires both hands.

sentence: Hermano, no vayas al banco ahora; ya está cerrado.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No vayas is the irregular negative tú command of ir. The affirmative command is ve.
note: The bank is already closed, explaining why the trip is unnecessary now.

sentence: Amigo, no seas grosero con Ana; ella solo pregunta tu nombre.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No seas is the negative tú command of ser, contrasting with affirmative sé. Here it requests appropriate behavior in this interaction.
note: Grosero means rude. The request concerns the friend's treatment of Ana during her question.

sentence: Hermana, no traigas pan a mi casa; ya tengo dos bolsas aquí.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No traigas uses irregular traig- in the negative tú command of traer. Aquí identifies the speaker's home as the endpoint.
note: The speaker already has two bags of bread at home.

sentence: Hermano, no des este recibo a Luis; Ana lo necesita para recoger el paquete.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No des is the irregular negative tú command of dar, contrasting with affirmative da. The receipt is the object and Luis is the prohibited recipient.
note: Lo refers to the receipt, which Ana needs for pickup.

sentence: Amiga, no sigas por esa calle; el museo está en la dirección contraria.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No sigas is the negative tú command of seguir, with stem sig-. Por esa calle identifies the route the listener should stop following.
note: Dirección contraria means the opposite direction here, rather than a postal address.

sentence: Amigo, no vuelvas a la oficina por el recibo; lo tengo aquí en la bolsa.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No vuelvas is the negative tú command of volver, retaining the o-to-ue stem change. A la oficina gives the return destination.
note: The return would be unnecessary because the speaker has the receipt.

sentence: Hermana, no busques tu camisa en el clóset; está en la bolsa de ropa limpia.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No busques is the negative tú command of buscar. The spelling changes c to qu before -es.
note: The speaker identifies where the shirt actually is.

sentence: Amigo, no pagues esa cuenta; yo ya pagué y tengo el recibo.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No pagues is the negative tú command of pagar. The spelling changes g to gu before -es.
note: The payment is already complete, and the speaker has its receipt.

sentence: Hermano, no empieces la tarea todavía; falta una página de las instrucciones.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No empieces is the negative tú command of empezar. It combines the e-to-ie stem change with z-to-c spelling before -es.
note: The missing instruction page explains why the task should not begin yet.

sentence: Hermana, no juegues con el balón en la sala; hay vasos en la mesa.
part_of_speech: negative particle and familiar singular command verb
grammar: No juegues is the negative tú command of jugar. It combines the u-to-ue stem change with gu before -es.
note: The ball game is unsuitable in this room because glasses are on the table.

sentence: Señor, hable más despacio, por favor; necesito su dirección para entregar el paquete.
grammar: Hable is the affirmative usted command of hablar. Regular -ar verbs use -e for this command; familiar affirmative habla uses -a.
register: Courteous singular usted address in a delivery service exchange.
note: Señor and su establish respectful address to one man.

sentence: Señora, coma un poco de sopa con nosotros; la comida ya está lista.
grammar: Coma is the affirmative usted command of comer. Regular -er verbs use -a in this command, contrasting with familiar come.
register: Respectful meal invitation to one woman.
note: The command functions as an invitation to share a ready meal.

sentence: Señora, abra su maleta para la revisión de equipaje, por favor.
grammar: Abra is the affirmative usted command of abrir. Regular -ir verbs use -a for this command, contrasting with familiar abre.
register: Courteous professional instruction to one traveler.
note: The baggage inspection supplies the professional purpose of the request.

sentence: Señor, escriba su fecha de nacimiento en este formulario de inscripción.
grammar: Escriba is the affirmative usted command of escribir. The requested information follows as the direct object.
note: The date of birth is the specific detail requested on the registration form.

sentence: Señora, ponga sus documentos en esta bandeja de recepción, por favor.
grammar: Ponga is the affirmative usted command of poner, using irregular pong-. Sus documentos are the objects to place.
note: Esta bandeja identifies the tray where the documents belong.

sentence: Señor, haga una copia de este documento para su inscripción, por favor.
grammar: Haga is the irregular affirmative usted command of hacer. Hacer una copia means make a copy.
note: The copy is needed for the addressee's registration.

sentence: Señora, venga aquí al mostrador; su pedido ya está listo.
grammar: Venga is the irregular affirmative usted command of venir. Aquí al mostrador specifies movement toward the speaker at the counter.
note: The customer's order is ready at the speaker's counter.

sentence: Señor, salga del hotel a la calle; su taxi está en la entrada.
grammar: Salga is the irregular affirmative usted command of salir. Del hotel names the place to leave, and a la calle names the destination.
note: The taxi's location explains where the guest should go.

sentence: Señora, diga su apellido por teléfono, por favor; necesito confirmar su cita.
grammar: Diga is the irregular affirmative usted command of decir. Su apellido specifies the information to say.
note: The worker needs the surname to confirm the appointment.

sentence: Señor, tenga su boleto listo; el camión sale en cinco minutos.
grammar: Tenga is the irregular affirmative usted command of tener. Tenga su boleto listo asks the listener to have his ticket ready.
note: The departure in five minutes makes having the ticket ready useful.

sentence: Señora, vaya a la ventanilla dos para recoger su boleto de autobús.
grammar: Vaya is the irregular affirmative usted command of ir. A la ventanilla dos identifies the destination.
note: The passenger needs window number two to collect her ticket.

sentence: Señor, sea paciente en la fila del banco; cada cliente tiene su turno.
grammar: Sea is the irregular affirmative usted command of ser. Paciente is the adjective expressing the requested attitude.
note: The request concerns waiting behavior in this bank line.

sentence: Señora, traiga su identificación aquí a recepción para recoger el paquete.
grammar: Traiga is the affirmative usted command of traer, using irregular traig-. Aquí a recepción locates the endpoint with the speaker.
note: The identification is needed to collect the package at reception.

sentence: Señor, dé este recibo al encargado de la caja, por favor.
grammar: Dé is the affirmative usted command of dar. Its written accent distinguishes the verb from unaccented preposition de, also visible in de la caja.
note: The receipt is transferred to the person in charge of the payment counter.

sentence: Señora, siga el pasillo hasta la sala de espera del consultorio.
grammar: Siga is the affirmative usted command of seguir, with e changing to i. El pasillo is the route to follow.
register: Respectful directions in a professional service setting.
note: Hasta marks the waiting room as the endpoint of the route.

sentence: Señor, vuelva a la clínica mañana a las diez para recoger sus resultados.
grammar: Vuelva is the affirmative usted command of volver, with o changing to ue. The destination and return time remain explicit.
note: The return is for collecting results at a stated time.

sentence: Señor, no hable por teléfono en la biblioteca; aquí necesitamos silencio.
part_of_speech: negative particle and formal singular command verb
grammar: No hable is the negative usted command of hablar. The verb form stays hable when no is added, unlike familiar habla versus no hables.
register: Respectful request to observe a shared-space rule.
note: The instruction concerns speaking on the phone inside the library.

sentence: Señora, no abra esa caja de la oficina; contiene documentos privados.
part_of_speech: negative particle and formal singular command verb
grammar: No abra is the negative usted command of abrir. Abra remains the command form with either affirmative or negative instructions.
note: Private documents inside the identified office box explain why it should remain closed.

sentence: Señor, no ponga su maleta en el pasillo del autobús; hay espacio debajo de su asiento.
part_of_speech: negative particle and formal singular command verb
grammar: No ponga is the negative usted command of poner. It retains irregular pong- and differs from familiar no pongas.
register: Respectful practical help to a passenger.
note: The speaker identifies available space under the passenger's seat.

sentence: Señora, no vaya a la ventanilla uno; está cerrada y puede recoger su boleto en la dos.
part_of_speech: negative particle and formal singular command verb
grammar: No vaya is the negative usted command of ir. The verb form stays vaya with no; familiar negative address instead uses no vayas.
note: La dos means window two, with ventanilla understood from the first clause.

sentence: Compañeros de clase, hablen de su familia en español.
grammar: Hablen addresses ustedes. The regular -ar plural command ends in -en, contrasting with singular usted hable.
register: Ordinary Mexican plural address to classmates.
note: Hablar de introduces the topic of conversation.

sentence: Hijos, abran las ventanas de la cocina; hace calor.
grammar: Abran is the affirmative ustedes command of abrir. Regular -ir commands use -an for plural address.
register: Direct household instruction to the speaker's children.
note: Hijos makes the plural family addressees explicit.

sentence: Ana y Luis, pongan los platos en la mesa; la comida está lista.
grammar: Pongan is the affirmative ustedes command of poner. It keeps irregular pong- and adds the plural command ending -an.
note: Los platos names the objects; en la mesa gives their destination.

sentence: Hijos, hagan la cena juntos; yo llego a las ocho.
grammar: Hagan is the affirmative ustedes command of hacer, using irregular hag-. Hacer la cena means make dinner.
note: Juntos asks the children to work together.

sentence: Amigos, vengan aquí a la mesa; hay café para todos.
grammar: Vengan is the affirmative ustedes command of venir. Aquí places the requested endpoint with the speaker.
note: The invitation brings the friends to the speaker's table.

sentence: Pasajeros, salgan del autobús a la banqueta, por favor.
grammar: Salgan is the affirmative ustedes command of salir. Del autobús names the vehicle to leave; a la banqueta names the destination.
register: Courteous instruction to a group of passengers.
note: Banqueta is the ordinary Mexican word for sidewalk here.

sentence: Compañeros, digan sus nombres para empezar la reunión.
grammar: Digan is the affirmative ustedes command of decir. Sus nombres specifies the information each addressee should provide.
note: The request begins the meeting with participants' names.

sentence: Pasajeros, tengan sus boletos listos; el camión sale en cinco minutos.
grammar: Tengan is the affirmative ustedes command of tener. Sus boletos listos requests that the passengers keep their tickets ready.
note: Listos agrees with plural masculine boletos.

sentence: Alumnos, vayan a la biblioteca para estudiar; el salón está cerrado.
grammar: Vayan is the affirmative ustedes command of ir. A la biblioteca identifies the destination.
register: Direct instruction to a student group.
note: The closed classroom explains the alternative study location.

sentence: Hijos, den estas llaves a su abuela Rosa; ella va a abrir la casa.
grammar: Den is the affirmative ustedes command of dar. Unlike singular usted dé, plural den has no written accent.
register: Ordinary family instruction to several children.
note: The keys are transferred to the named recipient, their grandmother Rosa.

sentence: Alumnos, no hablen ahora; necesito explicar la tarea.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No hablen is the negative ustedes command. Hablen remains the same verb form in affirmative and negative plural instructions.
note: The teacher needs quiet to explain the assignment.

sentence: Niños, no abran esta caja hasta el cumpleaños de Ana.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No abran prohibits opening in ustedes address. Hasta followed by the named event gives the limit of the instruction.
note: The box should remain closed until Ana's birthday.

sentence: Ana y Luis, no pongan sus bolsas en el pasillo; hay espacio debajo de la mesa.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No pongan is the negative ustedes command of poner. It retains irregular pong- and plural -an.
note: The speaker identifies space under the table as an alternative.

sentence: Vecinos, no hagan reparaciones esta noche; los niños necesitan dormir.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No hagan is the negative ustedes command of hacer. Hacer reparaciones means do repair work.
note: The request concerns tonight's repair work because the children need sleep.

sentence: Amigos, estoy en casa; no vengan aquí a las seis porque tengo una llamada de trabajo.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No vengan is the negative ustedes command of venir. Aquí refers to the speaker's explicitly stated location at home.
note: The work call makes six o'clock unsuitable for the visit.

sentence: Hijos, no salgan de la cocina durante la preparación de la cena; necesito su ayuda.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No salgan is the negative ustedes command of salir. De la cocina identifies the place the children should not leave.
note: The parent needs the children's help during dinner preparation.

sentence: Hijos, no digan la dirección de nuestra casa en el grupo de mensajes; es privada.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No digan is the negative ustedes command of decir. The following noun phrase identifies the information to keep private.
note: Privada describes the household's address.

sentence: Ana y Luis, no tengan sus teléfonos en la mesa durante la cena.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No tengan is the negative ustedes command of tener. Here tener concerns keeping controllable objects in a particular place.
note: The instruction concerns phone placement during dinner.

sentence: Pasajeros, no vayan a la ventanilla uno; sus boletos están en la dos.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No vayan is the negative ustedes command of ir. The incorrect destination follows a; the second clause identifies the correct window.
note: La dos means window two, with ventanilla understood.

sentence: Niños, no den este vaso a su abuela Rosa; está sucio.
part_of_speech: negative particle and plural command verb
grammar: No den is the negative ustedes command of dar. Den has no written accent in either affirmative or negative plural instructions.
note: The dirty glass is the item the children should not give to Rosa.

sentence: Ana, eres mi amiga; dime a qué hora empieza la clase.
part_of_speech: familiar singular affirmative command verb with attached speaker-recipient clitic
grammar: Dime attaches recipient me to affirmative tú command di. The whole form means tell me and has no written accent.
register: Familiar singular request to a friend.
note: The requested information is the class's starting time.

sentence: Luis, tú tienes mi libro; dámelo, por favor.
meaning: give it to me (familiar singular command)
part_of_speech: familiar singular affirmative command verb with attached recipient and masculine singular object clitics
grammar: Dámelo combines affirmative tú da, speaker-recipient me, and object lo referring to libro. The attached form requires an accent on dá.
note: Mi libro identifies the speaker's masculine singular item.

sentence: Ana, la camisa está limpia; ponla en tu cajón.
meaning: put it (familiar singular command; feminine object)
part_of_speech: familiar singular affirmative command verb with attached feminine singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Ponla attaches feminine object la to affirmative tú pon. La refers to camisa. Ponla needs no written accent.
note: En tu cajón gives the destination for the shirt.

sentence: Amigo, siéntate aquí en esta silla.
part_of_speech: familiar singular affirmative command verb with attached reflexive clitic
grammar: Siéntate attaches reflexive te to the affirmative tú command of sentarse. The verb has ie, and the attached form requires the accent in sién.
note: The instruction asks the friend to take the identified chair.

sentence: Amiga, no te pares de la silla; yo abro la puerta.
part_of_speech: second-person singular familiar reflexive clitic pronoun
grammar: Te stands between no and the negative tú command pares. It refers to the friend performing the action herself, contrasting with attached te in affirmative siéntate.
register: Familiar singular request to a female friend.
note: No te pares de la silla asks the friend to remain seated.

sentence: Señor, dígame a qué hora sale el autobús a Puebla, por favor.
part_of_speech: respectful singular affirmative command verb with attached speaker-recipient clitic
grammar: Dígame attaches recipient me to affirmative usted diga. The attached form requires the accent on dí.
note: Señor establishes respectful address to one man.

sentence: Señora, esa bolsa es mía; démela, por favor.
meaning: give it to me (respectful singular command; feminine object)
part_of_speech: respectful singular affirmative command verb with attached recipient and feminine singular object clitics
grammar: Démela combines affirmative usted dé, speaker-recipient me, and object la referring to bolsa. The complete form carries an accent on dé.
note: The bag belongs to the speaker, who is also the requested recipient.

sentence: Señoras y señores, siéntense en estas sillas; la reunión empieza ahora.
part_of_speech: plural affirmative command verb with attached reflexive clitic
grammar: Siéntense attaches reflexive se to the affirmative ustedes command of sentarse. Keep the command's n before se; the complete form requires the accent in sién.
register: Courteous plural address to an adult group.
note: Estas sillas identifies the seats offered to the group.

sentence: Amiga, este paquete es de Luis; no lo abras.
grammar: Lo replaces masculine singular paquete and stands between no and negative command abras. It precedes a negative command rather than attaching as in affirmative dámelo.
register: Familiar singular instruction to a friend.
note: Luis owns the package; the addressed friend is the person told not to open it.

sentence: Ana y Luis, esta llave es mía; no se la den a Mario.
meaning: it to him (the key to Mario)
part_of_speech: singular recipient replacement clitic and feminine singular direct-object clitic sequence
grammar: Se identifies Mario as recipient, replacing le before la. La replaces feminine singular llave. Both pronouns remain together between no and negative ustedes command den.
note: Ana and Luis are the addressees; Mario is the intended recipient of the prohibited transfer.

sentence: Esta chamarra es más cara que esa camisa.
grammar: Más before an adjective expresses a higher degree. In más cara que, the jacket's price is higher than the shirt's.
note: Más keeps its accent and does not change for gender or number.

sentence: Esta silla es menos cómoda que esa silla; prefiero esa.
grammar: Menos before an adjective expresses a lower degree. Menos cómoda que compares the comfort of the two chairs.
note: Esa in prefiero esa refers to the second chair.

sentence: Esta sopa está tan caliente como ese café.
part_of_speech: degree adverb in an equality comparison
grammar: Tan before an adjective pairs with visible como to express equal degree: tan caliente como means as hot as.
register: Neutral comparison of food and drink.
note: Tan does not agree with the gender of sopa.

sentence: Hoy tengo tanto trabajo como Ana; necesito ayuda.
grammar: Tanto quantifies masculine singular trabajo and pairs with como to compare equal amounts of work. Unlike tan before an adjective, tanto modifies a noun.
note: Trabajo refers to an amount of work here.

sentence: Esta receta lleva tanta leche como agua: un vaso de cada una.
grammar: Tanta agrees with feminine singular leche. Tanta leche como agua compares equal quantities of the two liquids.
note: One glass of each liquid makes the equal amounts explicit.

sentence: Mi hermana tiene tantos libros como yo: los dos tenemos diez.
grammar: Tantos agrees with masculine plural libros. With como, it compares equal numbers of countable books.
note: Each sibling has ten books.

sentence: En la sala hay tantas sillas como personas; nadie tiene que estar de pie.
grammar: Tantas agrees with feminine plural sillas. Tantas sillas como personas states that the chair count equals the person count.
note: The equal counts mean nobody needs to stand.

sentence: En esta caja hay más de cien hojas para la clase.
grammar: Más de introduces a number that the quantity exceeds. Cien is a numerical threshold; the sentence does not compare the box with another entity.
note: The box contains over one hundred sheets.

sentence: Prefiero el camión porque el viaje cuesta menos de cien pesos.
grammar: Menos de introduces a number that the amount falls below. The fare is below one hundred pesos.
note: Cien pesos is a price threshold.

sentence: Ana tiene más libros que Luis: ella tiene cinco y él tiene dos.
grammar: Que introduces Luis as the second person in the quantity comparison. Use que to compare their book counts; de introduces a numerical threshold in más de cinco.
note: Ana's five books exceed Luis's two.

sentence: Estos zapatos son de mejor calidad que esos; prefiero estos para caminar.
grammar: Mejor is the irregular comparative of bueno. Here it modifies singular calidad; que introduces the alternative.
note: The speaker chooses these shoes for their better quality.

sentence: Esta silla está en peor estado que la de la cocina; tiene una pata rota.
grammar: Peor is the irregular comparative of malo. Peor estado compares the condition of the two chairs.
note: The broken leg explains the unfavorable assessment.

sentence: Mi hermana es mayor que mi hermano: ella tiene treinta años y él tiene veinte.
grammar: Mayor que compares ages. Mayor has the same singular form for a woman and a man.
note: The sister is thirty and the brother is twenty.

sentence: Mi mamá es menor que mi papá: ella tiene cuarenta años y él tiene cincuenta.
grammar: Menor que compares ages and means younger than here. Menor does not change for gender.
note: The mother is forty and the father is fifty.

sentence: Mis hermanas cocinan mejor que yo; quiero aprender con ellas.
grammar: Mejor compares how well people cook. As an adverb modifying cocinan, it is invariant: it does not change for gender or number.
note: The comparison concerns cooking performance.

sentence: En el camión leo peor que en casa: el ruido es un problema.
grammar: Peor compares how well the speaker reads in two places. It modifies leo rather than describing a noun.
register: Neutral account of a practical difficulty.
note: Reading at home provides the benchmark.

sentence: Ana escribe más rápido que yo; termina los mensajes en un minuto.
grammar: Más modifies adverbial rápido to compare writing speed. It does not count messages or describe their properties.
note: Rápido describes how Ana writes.

sentence: En la biblioteca hablo menos fuerte que en casa; necesito silencio.
grammar: Menos modifies adverbial fuerte to compare speaking volume in two settings. Menos fuerte means less loudly.
register: Neutral explanation of behavior in a shared space.
note: The library and home provide the two speaking settings.

sentence: Ana lee tan despacio como yo; tenemos que practicar.
part_of_speech: degree adverb in an equality comparison
grammar: Tan before adverbial despacio pairs with como to compare equal reading speeds.
note: The sentence compares how Ana and the speaker actually read.

sentence: Mis hermanas trabajan tanto como yo: ocho horas al día.
grammar: Tanto modifies trabajan and pairs with como. Without a following quantified noun, adverbial tanto does not agree with hermanas.
note: The equal amount is eight working hours per day.

sentence: Esta mesa es mucho más grande que la de la cocina: aquí caben seis personas y allá solo dos.
grammar: Mucho intensifies más grande, expressing a large size difference. Mucho remains unchanged before the comparative.
note: The seating capacities make the large difference concrete.

sentence: Esta camisa es un poco más cara que esa: cuesta cinco pesos adicionales; prefiero esta.
grammar: Un poco limits the difference expressed by más cara. The comparison presents the extra cost as modest.
note: The additional five pesos specify the price difference.

sentence: Con las ventanas cerradas, el cuarto está mucho menos frío que con las ventanas abiertas; ya estoy cómodo.
grammar: Mucho intensifies menos frío, expressing a substantial reduction in coldness between two window conditions.
note: Closing the windows has made the speaker comfortable.

sentence: Señor, quiero otro café un poco menos caliente que este, por favor.
grammar: Un poco makes the requested decrease modest. Menos caliente que este compares the next coffee with the present cup.
register: Courteous service request to one man.
note: Este refers to the current coffee and supplies the comparison baseline.

sentence: Cada semana leo cada vez más rápido; ahora termino una página en un minuto.
grammar: Cada vez más before rápido expresses increasing speed over successive weeks.
note: Cada semana supplies the repeated occasions; ahora gives the current reading speed.

sentence: Antes tomaba tres cafés al día, luego dos y ahora uno: tomo cada vez menos café.
grammar: Cada vez menos expresses an amount that declines over time. Menos quantifies café here.
register: Neutral account of a changing daily habit.
note: Three coffees, then two, then one show the declining trajectory.

sentence: El camión azul es el más cómodo de estos tres; voy a tomar ese.
part_of_speech: masculine singular definite article and superlative degree adverb sequence
grammar: El más cómodo selects the highest degree of comfort within the three-bus group. El agrees with masculine singular camión.
note: De estos tres defines the comparison set.

sentence: De estas cuatro habitaciones, esta es la más tranquila; quiero dormir aquí.
part_of_speech: feminine singular definite article and superlative degree adverb sequence
grammar: La más tranquila selects the highest degree of quiet within the four-room set. La agrees with feminine singular habitación.
note: Esta identifies the room the speaker wants for sleeping.

sentence: De los diez ejercicios de la tarea, estos dos son los más difíciles; necesito ayuda.
part_of_speech: masculine plural definite article and superlative degree adverb sequence
grammar: Los más difíciles identifies two exercises at the highest difficulty level in the ten-exercise set. Los agrees with masculine plural ejercicios.
note: Estos dos identifies the difficult subset.

sentence: De las cinco mesas del salón, estas dos son las más grandes; aquí caben todos los platos.
part_of_speech: feminine plural definite article and superlative degree adverb sequence
grammar: Las más grandes identifies the largest two tables in the five-table group. Las agrees with feminine plural mesas.
register: Neutral preparation for a shared meal.
note: The tables' size makes them useful for holding all the plates.

sentence: De los tres cuartos de la casa, este es el menos ruidoso; voy a estudiar aquí.
part_of_speech: masculine singular definite article and superlative degree adverb sequence
grammar: El menos ruidoso selects the lowest noise level within the three-room set. El agrees with masculine singular cuarto.
note: Least noisy does not require the room to be completely silent.

sentence: De las tres clases de música, la de los sábados es la menos cara; puedo pagarla.
part_of_speech: feminine singular definite article and superlative degree adverb sequence
grammar: La menos cara selects the lowest price level among three classes. La agrees with feminine singular clase.
register: Neutral discussion of an affordable study option.
note: The Saturday class is the option the speaker can afford.

sentence: De los tres panes de la mesa, este es el mejor: está fresco y suave.
part_of_speech: masculine singular definite article and irregular superlative adjective sequence
grammar: El mejor expresses the highest quality within the three-bread set. Mejor replaces más bueno in this quality ranking.
note: Freshness and softness support the speaker's choice.

sentence: De las tres sopas del menú, esta es la peor: está fría y muy salada.
part_of_speech: feminine singular definite article and irregular superlative adjective sequence
grammar: La peor gives the lowest quality ranking within the three-soup set. La agrees with feminine singular sopa.
note: The cold temperature and excessive salt explain the judgment.

sentence: Este libro es uno de los más útiles del curso; lo uso todos los días.
grammar: Uno selects a single book from the course's group of most useful books. The adjective útiles is plural because it describes that group.
note: The expression places the book in a top group without calling it the sole best member.

sentence: Esta receta es una de las menos complicadas del libro; solo lleva tres ingredientes.
grammar: Una selects a single recipe from the book's least complicated group. Las and complicadas refer to feminine plural recetas.
note: Having only three ingredients supports the recipe's low complexity.

sentence: Tengo dos opciones: caminar o tomar el camión. ¿Cuál es mejor para llegar a tiempo?
grammar: Mejor functions predicatively in a question choosing between exactly two options. Do not add más before mejor in this comparison.
note: The choices are walking and taking the bus.

sentence: Antes trabajaba diez horas al día y ahora trabajo seis; trabajo menos que antes y duermo bien.
part_of_speech: comparative adverb phrase with a temporal benchmark
grammar: Menos que antes compares the present amount of work with an earlier amount. Antes supplies the time benchmark.
register: Neutral account of a changed work routine.
note: The working day has decreased from ten hours to six.

sentence: Mi papá está enfermo y vive conmigo; ahora necesito tu ayuda más que nunca.
grammar: Más que nunca compares the present degree of need with all earlier periods in the speaker's experience.
register: Personal request to a familiar singular listener.
note: The father's illness and presence at home explain the current need for help.

sentence: A esta hora, el camión está tan lleno como siempre; no hay asientos libres.
part_of_speech: adverbial comparative expression supplying a habitual benchmark
grammar: Como siempre supplies the usual degree of crowding as the benchmark in tan lleno como siempre.
note: Como siempre supplies the habitual benchmark rather than another vehicle.

sentence: Este cuaderno está baratísimo: cuesta cinco pesos y tiene cien hojas.
grammar: Baratísimo adds stressed -ísimo to the stem of barato. It expresses an exceptionally low price without ranking a comparison set.
note: The five-peso price motivates the evaluation.

sentence: Disculpe, el envío está carísimo: cuesta más que el libro.
grammar: Carísimo forms an absolute superlative from caro. The ending agrees with masculine singular envío.
note: The shipping charge exceeds the book's price.

sentence: Mamá, ¡este arroz está buenísimo! Quiero otro plato.
grammar: Buenísimo forms an absolute superlative from bueno and agrees with masculine singular arroz.
note: Asking for another plate reinforces the positive food evaluation.

sentence: Este café está malísimo: sabe a jabón. No lo voy a tomar.
grammar: Malísimo forms an absolute superlative from malo. It agrees with café and evaluates the drink's taste.
note: The coffee tastes of soap, and the speaker declines to drink it.

sentence: El camino a la clínica es larguísimo; necesitamos dos horas a pie para llegar.
grammar: Largo forms larguísimo with gu before í. The ending agrees with masculine singular camino.
note: The two-hour walk makes the route's length concrete.

sentence: Este queso está riquísimo; quiero otro pedazo.
grammar: Rico forms riquísimo with qu before í. Here rico evaluates flavor, and the ending agrees with queso.
note: The food context selects the tasty sense of rico.

sentence: Este ejercicio es facilísimo: solo hay que escribir tu nombre.
grammar: Fácil forms facilísimo. The original written accent disappears, and the new accent marks stress in -ísimo.
note: The task requires only writing a name.

sentence: Este examen es dificilísimo: tiene veinte preguntas y solo tenemos diez minutos.
grammar: Difícil forms dificilísimo. Stress shifts to the suffix, so the original accent is replaced by the accent in -ísimo.
note: Twenty questions in ten minutes make the task demanding.

sentence: Este cajón es pequeñísimo; mi libro no cabe.
grammar: Pequeño forms pequeñísimo by replacing final -o with -ísimo. The ñ remains, and the ending agrees with cajón.
note: The book's failure to fit makes the size problem concrete.

sentence: Queda poquísimo tiempo: el camión sale en dos minutos.
grammar: Poco forms poquísimo with qu before í. The masculine singular ending agrees with uncountable tiempo.
note: The bus departs in two minutes.

sentence: Ayer no llegué a mi cita por el retraso del camión.
grammar: Por introduces the cause of the missed appointment: the bus delay.
register: Neutral explanation of a travel problem.
note: The delay explains a completed disruption; por does not identify a route here.

sentence: Por el frío, dejé una chamarra en la mochila para usarla mañana.
grammar: Para introduces the intended use of the jacket. Por el frío gives the reason for the preparation; para usarla mañana gives its purpose.
note: Usarla refers to using or wearing the jacket tomorrow.

sentence: Entro a la casa por la puerta del patio.
grammar: With entrar, por introduces the opening used to enter. A la casa names the place entered.
note: The house is the destination; the patio door is the entry opening.

sentence: El camión sale para el centro y pasa por esta calle.
grammar: Sale para introduces the bus's intended destination. Pasa por identifies a street on its route.
note: Para marks where the bus is headed; por marks where it passes.

sentence: Ana no puede venir; hoy doy la clase por ella.
part_of_speech: preposition marking substitution for a person
grammar: Por ella identifies Ana as the absent person whose teaching the speaker takes over.
note: The speaker performs Ana's action in her place.

sentence: Yo trabajo horas extra para mi hija; ella necesita libros nuevos.
grammar: Para mi hija identifies the person intended to benefit from the speaker's extra work.
note: The daughter benefits from the effort; the speaker is not taking over her work.

sentence: Pagué cuarenta pesos por este libro.
grammar: Por links the amount paid to the product obtained in exchange.
note: Forty pesos is the total amount paid for this book.

sentence: No llamé a Ana; le mandé la dirección por internet.
grammar: Por introduces internet as the medium used to send the address.
note: The sentence contrasts sending information online with making a telephone call.

sentence: Voy a rentar un cuarto por dos noches, del lunes al miércoles.
grammar: Por introduces the planned length of the rental. Del lunes al miércoles supplies its endpoints.
note: This states a two-night rental, not how long an ongoing stay has lasted so far.

sentence: Todavía no termino la tarea; la maestra la necesita para el viernes.
grammar: Para el viernes establishes the deadline for having the homework ready.
note: The homework is still pending; para does not determine the verb tense by itself.

sentence: Ana, gracias por traer el pan; ya podemos cenar.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing the reason for thanks
grammar: After gracias, por introduces the action being thanked: bringing the bread.
register: Warm everyday thanks to a familiar person.
note: An infinitive can name the favor after gracias por.

sentence: Luis, perdón por llegar tarde; la clase ya empezó.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing the reason for an apology
grammar: After perdón, por introduces the action for which the speaker apologizes.
register: Everyday apology to a familiar person.
note: The class has already started, making the speaker's lateness explicit.

sentence: Aquí el estacionamiento cuesta veinte pesos por hora; enfrente cuesta treinta.
grammar: Por hora gives the unit used to calculate the parking charge.
note: Twenty pesos is the hourly rate, not necessarily the total bill.

sentence: La clínica está por el mercado; no sé la dirección exacta.
grammar: With static está, por el mercado gives an approximate area rather than a route.
register: Neutral explanation of an approximate location.
note: The speaker knows the general area but not the exact address.

sentence: Para Ana, este examen es fácil; Luis necesita ayuda.
grammar: Para Ana identifies whose perspective supports the evaluation fácil.
note: Ana is the evaluator, not the intended recipient of an object.

sentence: Somos seis en la mesa; hay dos tortillas por persona.
grammar: Por persona distributes the stated quantity to each individual at the table.
note: Two tortillas is each person's allocation.

sentence: Voy a comprar estos zapatos: son cómodos para caminar.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing an activity of suitability
grammar: Cómodos para caminar evaluates the shoes' suitability for walking.
register: Neutral explanation of a clothing choice.
note: The suitability of the shoes motivates the purchase.

sentence: Ana, no voy a ir a tu casa; hoy hablamos por teléfono.
grammar: Por teléfono specifies how the conversation takes place.
register: Everyday coordination with a familiar person.
note: The speaker proposes phone contact instead of visiting Ana's home.

sentence: El médico viene por la mañana, pero todavía no hay una hora exacta.
grammar: Por la mañana gives a broad daytime frame without specifying a clock time.
note: This differs from de la mañana after an exact hour.

sentence: ¡Ana lee muy bien para su edad: tiene solo cinco años!
grammar: Para su edad evaluates Ana's reading against expectations for someone of her age.
note: Her age supplies the benchmark; the exclamation conveys pleasant surprise.

sentence: Ana, ¿cómo se llama tu perro? Lo pregunto por curiosidad.
grammar: Por curiosidad identifies the motive for asking the dog's name.
note: The expression explains interest without suggesting a practical need for the information.

sentence: Mandé el mensaje a Luis por error; era para Ana.
grammar: Por error marks the sending to Luis as unintended. Para Ana identifies the intended recipient.
register: Neutral explanation of a messaging mistake.
note: Luis actually received a message intended for Ana.

sentence: Entre el curso de música y el de cocina, me decido por el de música.
grammar: Decidirse por introduces the option selected. Me decido marks the speaker's decision.
register: Neutral announcement of a study choice.
note: Por belongs to the choice construction here; it does not introduce a cause.

sentence: Este restaurante es famoso por su sopa; mucha gente viene a probarla.
grammar: Famoso por introduces the feature for which the restaurant is well known.
note: The soup is the reason for recognition, not an agent performing an action.

sentence: Luis está listo para salir; ya tiene las llaves en la mano.
meaning: to (the activity one is ready for)
grammar: Listo para introduces the upcoming activity for which Luis is ready.
note: Having the keys in hand supports Luis's readiness to leave.

sentence: Ana está preocupada por su papá; él está enfermo.
grammar: Preocupada por introduces the person who is the focus of Ana's concern.
note: Preocupada agrees with Ana; él refers to her father.

sentence: Esta llave sirve para abrir el cajón; la otra abre la puerta.
part_of_speech: preposition governed by servir in a function construction
grammar: Servir para introduces what an object is used to do, with the function expressed by an infinitive.
note: Sirve describes usefulness here, rather than serving food.

sentence: Ana tiene mi libro en su casa; paso por su casa a recogerlo esta tarde.
part_of_speech: preposition in a pickup-stop construction with pasar
grammar: Pasar por a place can mean stopping there during an outing. A recogerlo makes the pickup purpose explicit.
note: The speaker intends to collect the book, rather than merely travel past the house.

sentence: Busco mi llave; está por aquí, pero no la veo.
grammar: Por aquí indicates an approximate nearby area with static está.
note: Aquí alone can identify a location more directly; por aquí leaves the precise spot uncertain.

sentence: Voy a cerrar mi tienda para siempre; ya no voy a vender aquí.
grammar: Para siempre presents the planned closure as permanent.
register: Neutral announcement of a personal business decision.
note: The speaker does not describe a temporary closure or a deadline.

sentence: La casa todavía no está lista; por ahora vivo con mi hermana.
grammar: Por ahora limits the living arrangement to the present situation.
note: The house is not ready yet, so living with the sister is provisional.

sentence: Esperé una hora y por fin llegó el camión.
grammar: Por fin marks the bus's arrival as the awaited outcome after a delay.
note: The hour-long wait explains the sense of at last.

sentence: Hoy la escuela está cerrada; por eso voy a estudiar en casa.
grammar: Por eso introduces the consequence and points back to the school's closure.
note: Eso refers to the explicit preceding cause, not to a physical object.

sentence: Ana, tienes un cepillo junto a los zapatos. ¿Para qué sirve?
grammar: Para qué asks the purpose or function of the brush. Qué retains its interrogative accent.
register: Everyday inquiry to a familiar person.
note: The question asks the brush's function, rather than the cause of an event.

sentence: Vienen seis personas a cenar; necesito por lo menos seis platos, quizá más.
part_of_speech: adverbial phrase marking a lower bound
grammar: Por lo menos sets six as the minimum number of plates needed.
note: Quizá más leaves open the possibility of needing additional plates.

sentence: La cita es mañana a las diez; voy a tener los papeles listos para entonces.
part_of_speech: temporal prepositional phrase with an anaphoric deadline
grammar: Para entonces sets a deadline by referring back to tomorrow's ten o'clock appointment. Voy a expresses the speaker's plan.
note: Entonces refers to the appointment time already stated.

sentence: Necesito la dirección por escrito; quiero guardar el mensaje.
grammar: Por escrito specifies that the address must be communicated in written form.
note: A written message lets the speaker keep a record of the address.

sentence: Siempre desayuno huevos; hoy voy a comer fruta para variar.
grammar: Para variar presents eating fruit as an intentional change from the usual breakfast.
register: Everyday discussion of a food choice.
note: The visible routine supports the literal wish for variety; there is no ironic complaint.

sentence: —Ana, ¿puedes ayudarme con la tarea? —Sí, por supuesto; tengo tiempo.
grammar: Por supuesto reinforces the affirmative response to a request for help.
register: Friendly assurance in familiar singular address.
note: Ana confirms her willingness and says she has time.

sentence: Este teléfono no enciende ni recibe llamadas; no sirve para nada.
grammar: In no sirve para nada, the phrase denies any practical usefulness. Postverbal nada combines with preverbal no.
register: Everyday complaint about a failed device.
note: The phone neither turns on nor receives calls, supporting the judgment that it is useless.

sentence: No puedo lavar los platos por falta de agua; hoy no hay agua en casa.
grammar: Por falta de introduces a missing resource as the cause of a problem.
note: The missing water prevents washing the dishes.

sentence: Este teléfono es para uso personal; en la oficina tenemos otro para todos.
grammar: Para uso personal specifies use by an individual rather than the office group.
note: The office has a different phone available to everyone.

sentence: La consulta con el médico es mañana; hoy tengo que pagar por adelantado.
grammar: Por adelantado places the payment before the service.
register: Neutral discussion of an appointment payment.
note: Payment is today, while the medical appointment is tomorrow.

sentence: Ana, vamos a preparar la sopa; para empezar, lava los tomates.
grammar: Para empezar introduces the first action in preparing the soup.
note: Only the opening-step expression is hidden; washing the tomatoes remains visible.

sentence: Luis y yo vamos a comer juntos, pero vamos a pagar por separado: cada uno paga su comida.
grammar: Por separado describes independent payments despite a shared meal.
note: Each person pays for their own food.

sentence: En clase practicamos el diálogo por parejas: Ana con Luis y Marta conmigo.
grammar: Por parejas organizes participants into groups of two.
note: Ana works with Luis, and Marta works with the speaker. The expression specifies grouping rather than alternating turns or an amount per person.

sentence: Ayer rompí un vaso por accidente; no fue a propósito.
grammar: Por accidente presents the breakage as unintended.
register: Everyday explanation of a household mishap.
note: The phrase describes an accidental physical mishap, rather than selecting the wrong recipient or item.

sentence: Ana y Luis usan la computadora por turnos: primero Ana y después Luis, nunca los dos al mismo tiempo.
grammar: Por turnos describes alternating use rather than simultaneous use.
register: Neutral explanation of a shared resource.
note: Ana uses the computer first, followed by Luis.

sentence: Revisé el cajón: está limpio por dentro y no tiene polvo en el fondo.
grammar: Por dentro identifies the interior area whose cleanliness was checked.
note: The phrase locates the clean surfaces inside the drawer.

sentence: Revisé la bolsa: está limpia por fuera, pero tiene polvo por dentro.
grammar: Por fuera identifies the bag's exterior, contrasted with por dentro.
note: The exterior is clean, while the interior is dusty.

sentence: Ayer me quejé de la falta de agua en el hotel; no pude bañarme.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb with governed preposition
grammar: Quejarse de takes de before the problem being complained about. Me belongs to the pronominal verb.
register: Neutral account of a service complaint.
note: The complaint concerns the missing water and its practical consequence.

sentence: Hoy me enteré de un cambio de horario por un aviso: la clase empieza a las diez.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb with governed preposition
grammar: Enterarse de introduces information newly learned. The preterite marks today's completed discovery.
note: The notice provides the information about the changed class time.

sentence: Estaba tranquilo, pero me preocupé por mi papá cuando no llegó a casa a la hora de siempre.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb with governed preposition
grammar: Me preocupé por presents the onset of concern. Estaba tranquilo supplies the earlier calm state.
note: The speaker becomes worried because his father does not arrive at the usual time.

sentence: Después de una clase de cocina, me interesé por esa actividad y busqué otro curso.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb with governed preposition
grammar: Interesarse por makes the interested person the subject. Me is part of the pronominal verb, unlike the experiencer in me interesa.
register: Neutral account of a developing interest.
note: Esa actividad refers to cooking.

sentence: Esperé una hora sin hacer nada y me aburrí.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Me aburrí presents becoming bored during the wait. Me belongs to aburrirse.
note: The hour with nothing to do provides the setting for the boredom.

sentence: Ayer Ana y yo nos divertimos con un juego de mesa en casa.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Nos belongs to divertirse and matches Ana y yo. Ayer establishes the completed past reading of divertimos.
register: Friendly account of a shared activity.
note: The verb expresses enjoying the activity, rather than entertaining another person.

sentence: Ayer me enojé porque la impresora no funcionaba y necesitaba imprimir un aviso.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Me enojé marks becoming upset. The imperfect forms describe the equipment problem and need present at that time.
note: The nonworking printer is the stated reason for the reaction.

sentence: Hoy limpié toda la casa y me cansé; después descansé un rato.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Me cansé expresses becoming tired after the household effort, rather than merely being in a tired state.
note: Today's completed cleaning and rest naturally use the simple preterite here.

sentence: El lunes me enfermé y no fui al trabajo; tenía fiebre.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Me enfermé marks becoming ill on Monday. Tenía describes the accompanying fever.
note: The speaker reports an illness and absence from work without identifying its cause.

sentence: El lunes tenía un resfriado, pero ya me mejoré y hoy estoy bien.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Mejorarse here means recovering from illness. Me identifies the speaker as the person recovering.
note: The earlier cold and present wellbeing establish the recovery meaning.

sentence: Ana y Luis se saludan el uno al otro antes de la clase.
part_of_speech: reciprocal clitic with third-person plural present indicative verb
grammar: Saludan supplies the plural greeting action; se makes it reciprocal. El uno al otro explicitly confirms mutuality.
register: Neutral description of a social routine.
note: Each person greets the other person.

sentence: Ana y Luis son hermanos; los dos quieren un abrazo y se abrazan.
part_of_speech: reciprocal clitic with third-person plural present indicative verb
grammar: Abrazan expresses hugging; reciprocal se indicates that Ana and Luis hug one another.
note: Both siblings want the hug; neither is described as hugging themself.

sentence: Ana y Luis se ayudan el uno al otro con la tarea de español.
part_of_speech: reciprocal clitic with third-person plural present indicative verb
grammar: Ayudan supplies the helping action; se and el uno al otro make the help mutual.
note: Ana helps Luis, and Luis helps Ana.

sentence: Ana y Luis se conocen bien; son amigos de la infancia.
part_of_speech: reciprocal clitic with third-person plural present indicative verb
grammar: Se makes conocer reciprocal between Ana and Luis. The present describes an existing acquaintance.
note: Their childhood friendship establishes an existing relationship rather than a first meeting.

sentence: Ana y Luis tienen una reunión de trabajo; se ven hoy a las cinco en el café.
part_of_speech: reciprocal clitic with third-person plural present indicative verb
grammar: Se ven describes the two people seeing one another at an arranged meeting. The present states today's arrangement.
note: The phrase describes a meeting, rather than functioning as a farewell.

sentence: Ayer la puerta se abrió con el viento; nadie la tocó.
part_of_speech: pronominal marker with third-person singular preterite verb
grammar: Se abrió presents the door's change from closed to open. The wind supplies the stated cause.
register: Everyday account of a household event.
note: The door is the changing object; nobody is described as opening it by hand.

sentence: Anoche la ventana se cerró por una corriente de aire.
part_of_speech: pronominal marker with third-person singular preterite verb
grammar: Se cerró presents a change in the window's position. Por introduces the draft that caused it.
note: The sentence describes the window closing from a draft.

sentence: Hace calor y el hielo se derrite en el vaso.
part_of_speech: pronominal marker with third-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Se derrite describes ice changing into liquid. Derretirse has e-to-i stem change in this present form.
note: The subject is the ice undergoing the change.

sentence: La sopa se enfría en la mesa mientras Ana y Luis esperan las tortillas.
part_of_speech: pronominal marker with third-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Se enfría describes the soup losing heat. The written accent belongs to enfría.
note: The soup cools while the diners wait; no person is described as cooling it.

sentence: El agua de la botella se calienta al sol; ya está tibia.
part_of_speech: pronominal marker with third-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Se calienta describes the water gaining heat. Calentarse has e-to-ie stem change in this present form.
note: The sun is the visible heat source, and tibia describes the water's resulting temperature.

sentence: Normalmente lavo los platos después de cenar, pero ahora estoy lavando una olla.
grammar: Estoy with a gerund presents an action in progress now. Lavo with normalmente describes the routine.
register: Everyday account of a current household task.
note: The auxiliary agrees with the speaker; lavando supplies the ongoing action.

sentence: Luis, ¿tú estás escribiendo la dirección ahora? Necesito mandar el paquete hoy.
grammar: Estás agrees with familiar singular tú and combines with escribiendo to ask about writing in progress.
note: Luis is the person being asked about the current writing task.

sentence: Ana está preparando la cena en este momento; no puede contestar el teléfono.
grammar: Está agrees with the named singular subject Ana and introduces preparation currently in progress.
note: En este momento explicitly anchors the activity to now.

sentence: Ana y yo estamos moviendo la mesa ahora; necesitamos ayuda porque pesa mucho.
grammar: Estamos agrees with Ana y yo, a group including the speaker, and presents their shared action as ongoing.
register: Everyday coordination of a household task.
note: The heavy table explains the group's need for help.

sentence: Ana y Luis están pintando el cuarto ahora; la pintura todavía está húmeda.
grammar: Están agrees with the two named painters and presents their activity as in progress now.
note: The sentence reports current painting activity rather than a habitual work schedule.

sentence: Ahora estoy hablando con mi mamá por teléfono.
grammar: Hablar forms its gerund with -ando: hablando. Visible estoy makes the conversation an ongoing action.
register: Everyday description of a current conversation.
note: Con mi mamá identifies the person the speaker is talking with.

sentence: Ana y yo estamos comiendo sopa ahora; todavía está caliente.
grammar: Comer forms its gerund with -iendo: comiendo. Estamos places the shared meal in progress.
note: The final está caliente describes the soup's temperature.

sentence: Normalmente vivo en Puebla, pero este mes estoy viviendo en casa de mi hermana en Toluca.
grammar: Vivir forms its gerund with -iendo: viviendo. Estoy viviendo frames the current residence as temporary here.
note: The speaker's usual home is in Puebla; this month's accommodation is in Toluca.

sentence: Luis está leyendo el mensaje en su teléfono ahora.
grammar: Leer has the gerund leyendo, with y. It combines with visible está for reading in progress.
register: Neutral update about a current activity.
note: The gerund has no written accent.

sentence: Estoy oyendo golpes en la puerta ahora; ¿tú también los oyes?
grammar: Oír has the gerund oyendo, with y. Estoy oyendo describes sounds being perceived now.
register: Everyday check about an audible disturbance.
note: Oír expresses perceiving the sounds; it does not require deliberate listening.

sentence: Ahora estoy yendo al trabajo en camión; ya pasamos la escuela.
grammar: Ir has the irregular gerund yendo. Estoy yendo presents the journey as currently underway.
note: The speaker is already on the bus, traveling to work.

sentence: Ana está pidiendo la cuenta al mesero ahora.
grammar: Pedir changes e to i in its gerund: pidiendo. La cuenta is the requested item; al mesero identifies the person being asked.
note: Pedir requests an item here.

sentence: Luis normalmente duerme de noche, pero ahora está durmiendo después de su turno.
grammar: Dormir changes o to u in durmiendo. Está durmiendo describes current sleep; duerme describes the usual schedule.
note: His current sleep follows a work shift.

sentence: Ana está diciendo «gracias» a la enfermera en este momento.
grammar: Decir has the gerund diciendo, with e changing to i. The quoted word supplies the content being spoken.
register: Neutral description of a courteous exchange.
note: A la enfermera identifies the person receiving Ana's thanks.

sentence: Estoy en casa; Luis está trayendo el pan hasta aquí.
grammar: Traer has the gerund trayendo, with y. Está trayendo presents the bread's transport toward the speaker as ongoing.
note: Aquí refers to the home where the speaker is.

sentence: Ahora estamos siguiendo la ruta marcada en el mapa hacia la clínica.
grammar: Seguir changes e to i in siguiendo. The direct object la ruta identifies the route being followed.
note: The group is currently following the marked route toward the clinic.

sentence: Mi papá está construyendo una mesa para la cocina; todavía faltan dos patas.
grammar: Construir forms the gerund construyendo with y. Está construyendo presents the project as unfinished.
note: The missing legs make the table's unfinished state explicit.

sentence: Está cayendo mucha lluvia ahora; la calle ya está mojada.
grammar: Caer has the gerund cayendo, with y. Está cayendo describes rain falling now.
note: The wet street is a visible present result of the rain.

sentence: Ana está viniendo a mi casa en taxi ahora; yo la espero aquí.
grammar: Venir has the irregular gerund viniendo. Está viniendo presents Ana's movement toward the speaker as underway.
note: The speaker is waiting at the destination, their own home.

sentence: Mi planta se está muriendo: tiene todas las hojas secas.
grammar: Morir changes o to u in muriendo. Se está muriendo uses everyday pronominal morirse to describe decline in progress.
note: The plant's dry leaves provide visible evidence of its decline.

sentence: Ahora estoy sintiendo frío en las manos por el agua helada.
grammar: Sentir changes e to i in sintiendo. Estoy sintiendo frames the bodily sensation as occurring now.
note: Frío is the sensation; the very cold water supplies its cause.

sentence: Antes comía fuera; estos días estoy prefiriendo comer en casa cada noche.
grammar: Preferir changes e to i in prefiriendo. The progressive presents a temporary tendency across recent repeated choices.
register: Conversational account of changing meal preferences.
note: Estos días and cada noche frame several recent choices, rather than one isolated preference.

sentence: Ana está sonriendo al ver a su hermana en la entrada.
grammar: Sonreír has the gerund sonriendo, without a written accent. Está sonriendo describes a visible ongoing reaction.
note: Seeing her sister at the entrance prompts Ana's smile.

sentence: El libro es de Ana; lo estoy leyendo aquí.
grammar: Lo refers to libro and precedes progressive auxiliary estoy. Estoy leyéndolo is another placement with the same meaning.
register: Neutral conversation about a borrowed or shared book.
note: In leyéndolo, lo attaches to the gerund and the written accent preserves its stress.

sentence: Ahora le estoy dando un libro a Ana.
grammar: Recipient le precedes progressive auxiliary estoy. Un libro remains the direct object, and a Ana names the recipient.
register: Neutral description of a current transfer.
note: Le estoy dando and estoy dándole allow the same recipient reading.

sentence: Yo me estoy lavando las manos con jabón.
grammar: Me refers back to subject yo and precedes progressive auxiliary estoy. Estoy lavándome is an alternative placement.
note: The speaker washes their own hands. In le estoy dando, the clitic instead identifies a separate recipient.

sentence: Ana, estoy esperándote en la entrada del café.
part_of_speech: gerund with attached familiar singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Esperándote combines gerund esperando with direct-object te referring to Ana. The written accent preserves the gerund's stress.
note: The speaker is waiting; Ana is the person being waited for.

sentence: Luis está lavándose con jabón en la regadera.
part_of_speech: gerund with attached third-person reflexive clitic
grammar: Lavándose combines gerund lavando with reflexive se referring to Luis. The written accent preserves the gerund's stress.
note: Luis is washing himself in the shower. Se refers back to Luis.

sentence: Ana necesita el lápiz; Luis está dándoselo a Ana ahora.
part_of_speech: gerund with attached recipient and direct-object clitics
grammar: Dándoselo combines dando, recipient se replacing le, and masculine object lo. The written accent preserves stress; se and lo stay together.
note: Luis gives the pencil; Ana receives it. Lo refers to el lápiz.

sentence: Normalmente trabajo en la oficina, pero esta semana estoy trabajando en casa.
grammar: Trabajar forms its gerund with -ando: trabajando. Estoy trabajando frames this week's work arrangement as temporary; trabajo states the regular arrangement.
note: The progressive can describe a temporary current arrangement extending beyond the exact moment of speaking.

sentence: Ya hay café caliente; acabo de prepararlo.
grammar: Present acabo de with an infinitive expresses very recent completion. Prepararlo names the completed action.
note: The freshly prepared hot coffee supplies a present result.

sentence: Ana acabó de limpiar el baño a las seis y después salió.
grammar: Preterite acabó de with limpiar marks the completion of cleaning at a bounded past time.
note: Here acabó de means finished doing. Present acabo de commonly expresses having just done something.

sentence: Ya tengo el jabón y empiezo a lavar los platos.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present onset component with linking preposition
grammar: Empezar takes a before an infinitive naming the activity begun. Empiezo has the present e-to-ie stem change.
note: Lavar los platos remains the activity that is starting.

sentence: La maestra abrió el libro y comenzó a explicar la tarea.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite onset component with linking preposition
grammar: Comenzar takes a before the infinitive naming the activity begun. Comenzó marks the onset as a completed past event.
note: Comenzar a and empezar a both express starting an activity.

sentence: Llegó mi hermana y me puse a preparar la cena.
part_of_speech: first-person singular pronominal preterite onset component
grammar: Ponerse a with an infinitive expresses taking up an activity. Me puse is its first-person preterite component.
register: Everyday account of responding to an arrival.
note: The speaker begins preparing dinner after their sister arrives.

sentence: Llamé a Ana a las nueve y volví a llamar a las diez; no contestó.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite repetition component with linking preposition
grammar: Volver a with an infinitive repeats the named activity. Volví a llamar means I called again.
register: Neutral account of attempted phone contact.
note: The nine o'clock call is the explicit earlier occurrence; this use does not describe returning to a place.

sentence: Antes tomaba café por la noche, pero dejé de tomarlo porque no dormía bien.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite cessation component with linking preposition
grammar: Dejar de with an infinitive expresses stopping an activity. The earlier routine is supplied by antes tomaba.
register: Everyday account of a changed habit.
note: The speaker stops the nighttime coffee habit because sleep was poor.

sentence: Tengo mucho trabajo, pero no dejo de visitar a mi mamá cada domingo.
part_of_speech: negated first-person singular present persistence component
grammar: No dejar de with an infinitive expresses continuing an activity here. Negation reverses the cessation meaning of dejar de.
register: Everyday statement of a maintained family routine.
note: The visits continue despite the heavy workload.

sentence: Terminé de lavar los platos y después preparé la cena.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite completion component with linking preposition
grammar: Terminar de takes an infinitive naming the completed activity. Terminé de lavar marks completion before the next action.
note: The dishes are washed before dinner preparation begins.

sentence: Ana empezó a estudiar a las seis y sigue estudiando ahora.
grammar: Seguir with a gerund expresses continuation. Sigue estudiando means that Ana keeps studying.
note: Seguir takes a gerund directly here; its earlier route-following use takes a route as its object.

sentence: Ya es de noche, pero Luis continúa preparando la clase de mañana.
grammar: Continuar combines directly with a gerund to express continuation. Continúa retains a written accent on ú.
note: Continúa preparando and sigue preparando both express continued preparation.

sentence: Poco a poco voy entendiendo las llamadas en español.
grammar: Ir with a gerund presents an activity as developing gradually. Voy entendiendo expresses increasing understanding.
note: Poco a poco makes the gradual development explicit; voy does not express physical travel here.

sentence: Ya tengo las llaves en la mano y estoy a punto de salir de casa.
grammar: Estar a punto de takes an infinitive and presents its action as imminent.
note: Having the keys in hand supports the speaker's immediate readiness to leave.

sentence: El baño está por limpiar; todavía está sucio.
grammar: Estar por with an infinitive presents an action as still pending here. Limpiar identifies the unfinished task.
note: The bathroom is still dirty, so its cleaning remains undone.

sentence: Tengo pensado visitar a mi hermana el sábado; ya compré el boleto.
