grammar: Tener pensado takes an infinitive to express a planned intention. Visitar names the intended activity.
note: The purchased ticket is a concrete preparation for the planned visit.

sentence: La entrada es gratis; no tienes por qué pagar, Ana.
meaning: you have no reason or obligation to
part_of_speech: negated familiar singular present necessity-or-justification component
grammar: No tener por qué takes an infinitive and denies a reason or obligation to perform it. Qué carries a written accent in this expression.
note: Free admission explains why Ana need not pay.

sentence: Ayer perdí la llave y tuve que esperar a mi hermana en la entrada.
grammar: Tuve que with an infinitive expresses necessity in one bounded past incident. Tenía que can instead describe a customary past obligation.
register: Neutral account of a practical problem.
note: Losing the key creates the situational need to wait.

sentence: El camión salió a las ocho; alcancé a subir un minuto antes.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite achievement component with linking preposition
grammar: Alcanzar a with an infinitive expresses managing an action within the available time here. Alcancé changes z to c before é.
note: The speaker boarded one minute before the bus departed.

sentence: Primero leía frases cortas; con la práctica, llegué a leer un libro completo en español.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite attainment component with linking preposition
grammar: Llegar a with an infinitive expresses reaching an achievement after development. Llegué uses gu before é.
note: Reading short phrases is the earlier stage; reading a complete book is the later achievement.

sentence: Tardé diez minutos en abrir la puerta.
meaning: to (linking a time taken to an action)
grammar: Tardar takes en before an infinitive naming the action that takes time. Diez minutos supplies the measured interval.
register: Neutral account of a delayed practical task.
note: En links tardé to abrir here; it does not introduce a location.

sentence: Ya lavé los platos; solo queda por limpiar la mesa.
grammar: Quedar por takes an infinitive naming the pending action. Here cleaning the table remains after washing the dishes.
note: This use concerns unfinished work rather than an object's location.

sentence: El texto tiene diez páginas: ya leí ocho y me faltan por leer dos.
grammar: Faltar por takes an infinitive identifying unfinished work. Faltan agrees with the two remaining pages; me identifies the reader.
note: Eight of ten pages are finished, leaving two to read.

sentence: La camisa está sin lavar; por eso no está lista para mañana.
grammar: Estar sin followed by an infinitive describes a current state in which the action has not been performed. The shirt has not been washed.
note: The unwashed state explains why the shirt is not ready.

sentence: Estos días ando leyendo anuncios de trabajo en internet, un rato cada tarde.
grammar: Andar with a gerund presents activity spread across a recent period. Ando leyendo describes repeated reading of job advertisements these days.
note: The online reading happens each afternoon; andar does not describe walking here.

sentence: Ya pasó una semana y sigo sin recibir el paquete.
grammar: Seguir sin takes an infinitive and expresses the continued absence of its action. Sigo is the first-person present of seguir.
note: Seguir with a gerund continues an activity; seguir sin with an infinitive continues its absence.

sentence: Para preparar la cena, empiezo por lavar las verduras.
grammar: Empezar por with an infinitive selects the first step in a larger task.
note: Empezar a marks an activity's onset; empezar por identifies which action comes first.

sentence: Busqué la llave en la mesa y en la bolsa; terminé por llamar a mi hermana.
grammar: Terminar por with an infinitive introduces an eventual outcome after earlier actions or attempts.
register: Neutral account of a household problem.
note: Calling the sister follows the searches. Terminar de would express finishing an activity.

sentence: Leí las instrucciones dos veces, pero no termino de entender el primer paso para abrir la puerta.
part_of_speech: negated first-person singular present periphrastic component
grammar: No terminar de with entender expresses incomplete understanding despite attempts to understand. It goes beyond simply saying that an activity has not finished.
note: The speaker has read the instructions twice but still does not fully understand the first step.

sentence: Los domingos suelo preparar sopa para mi familia.
grammar: Soler takes a bare infinitive to describe a usual action. Suelo has the present o-to-ue stem change.
note: The Sunday schedule describes a habit rather than an activity happening at this moment.

sentence: Mi hermana me deja usar su computadora para la tarea.
grammar: Dejar takes a person complement and a bare infinitive to express permission. Me is the person allowed to use the computer.
note: There is no de before usar. Dejar de instead expresses stopping an action.

sentence: Trabajo en esta escuela desde enero y todavía estoy aquí.
grammar: Desde introduces the starting point of work that continues now. Enero supplies a calendar point rather than an elapsed quantity.
note: The present trabajo and todavía estoy aquí establish continuation.

sentence: Vivo aquí desde antes de la mudanza de Ana.
grammar: Desde antes de places the beginning of the current residence before the named move.
note: The exact starting date is unstated; the residence already existed before Ana's move.

sentence: En enero conocí a Rosa; desde entonces hablamos cada domingo.
grammar: Desde entonces recovers its starting point from the preceding event: meeting Rosa in January. The present hablamos describes their continuing routine.
register: Neutral account of a personal relationship.
note: Entonces refers to the January meeting.

sentence: El curso empezó en marzo; estudio con este grupo desde el principio.
grammar: Desde el principio marks participation from the outset of the course through the present.
note: The speaker joined at the course's beginning rather than at a later stage.

sentence: Vivo con mi hermana desde que llegué a Puebla.
grammar: Desde que introduces a clause naming the onset event. Preterite llegué marks the completed arrival; present vivo gives the continuing residence.
note: The arrival is the starting point for living with the sister.

sentence: Mi hermana y yo comemos juntas los viernes desde que vivimos en la misma ciudad.
grammar: Desde que with present vivimos introduces a living situation that continues now. It establishes the period in which the Friday meal routine applies.
note: Both the shared city of residence and the repeated meals remain current.

sentence: Estudio español desde hace seis meses y todavía voy a clase.
grammar: Desde hace introduces an elapsed quantity for a situation continuing in the present. Seis meses measures duration.
note: Desde enero gives a starting point; desde hace seis meses gives elapsed time.

sentence: Cuando Ana llegó a la oficina, yo trabajaba allí desde hacía dos meses.
meaning: for (an elapsed interval up to a past point)
grammar: Desde hacía measures duration up to Ana's past arrival. Imperfect trabajaba supplies the work situation continuing at that past reference point.
note: The two months are measured at Ana's arrival, rather than from the present.

sentence: Devolví las llaves hace dos días; Ana ya las tiene.
grammar: Hace followed by a time quantity locates a completed event before now. Devolví presents returning the keys as finished.
note: Hace dos días means two days ago; desde hace dos días would introduce a continuing interval.

sentence: Cuando llegó Luis, hacía dos horas que yo esperaba en la entrada.
grammar: Hacía measures elapsed time at Luis's past arrival. Que links the two-hour quantity to the background waiting situation.
note: Hacía remains singular. The duration is measured at the arrival rather than now.

sentence: Hace tres años que estudio música; todavía voy a clases.
grammar: Hace with a time quantity and que introduces the duration of a present ongoing situation. Estudio identifies the speaker's continuing activity.
note: The present activity continues now; this is different from a completed event followed by hace meaning ago.

sentence: Ana ya está en casa; no hace ni una hora que llegó.
grammar: No hace negates the elapsed-time threshold. With ni una hora, the sentence says that less than one hour has passed since Ana arrived.
note: Ni adds even: it has not even been an hour.

sentence: Hace dos meses que no hablo con mi hermano; todavía espero su llamada.
grammar: Hace with a duration and que no measures an absence continuing to now. No hablo states the missing contact.
note: The two months measure how long the siblings have gone without speaking.

sentence: Hace una semana que devolví el libro a Ana.
meaning: since (linking elapsed time to an event)
grammar: Que links hace una semana to the completed event devolví el libro. The whole sentence measures time since that event.
register: Neutral update about a borrowed item.
note: Que introduces an event clause here and does not modify a noun.

sentence: Trabajaba de noche hasta hace un mes; ahora trabajo de día.
grammar: Hasta hace introduces an endpoint measured backward from now. Un mes gives the interval since the former night-work routine ended.
note: The present daytime schedule makes the change explicit.

sentence: Recientemente cambié de trabajo; ahora doy clases en otra escuela.
grammar: Recientemente places the completed job change in the recent past without specifying an exact interval. Cambié uses the simple preterite naturally here.
note: The new teaching job supplies the current consequence.

sentence: Ayer cuidé a mi sobrino durante dos horas; después llegó su mamá.
grammar: Durante introduces the bounded duration of a finished activity. Cuidé presents the two-hour care period as complete.
note: Dos horas measures the activity's span; desde would introduce a starting point.

sentence: Terminé la tarea en veinte minutos; ya está lista.
grammar: En with a time quantity states how long reaching completion took. Terminé and lista make the finished result explicit.
note: Durante measures an activity's span; en here measures time to its completed outcome.

sentence: Ayer trabajé de ocho a doce y luego salí.
grammar: De marks the beginning of the bounded de ocho a doce interval. A introduces its endpoint.
note: Both clock times remain visible: work began at eight and ended at twelve.

sentence: Ayer esperé a Luis desde las dos hasta las tres; llegó a las tres.
grammar: Hasta introduces the endpoint of the finished waiting interval. Desde las dos supplies its start.
register: Neutral account of a delayed arrival.
note: Luis's arrival at three explains the end of the wait.

sentence: En mayo compré un carro; hasta entonces iba al trabajo en camión, pero ahora voy en carro.
grammar: Hasta entonces refers back to the May car purchase as the endpoint of the former bus commute.
note: Iba gives the earlier routine; ahora voy states the changed current routine.

sentence: Ana, ¿desde cuándo trabajas en esta escuela?
grammar: Desde cuándo asks for the starting point of Ana's current work situation. Cuándo carries an interrogative accent.
note: A starting month or date can answer this question.

sentence: Ana, ¿desde hace cuánto estudias música? Todavía vas a clases cada lunes.
grammar: Desde hace cuánto asks for the elapsed quantity of time during which Ana has studied music and continues to do so.
note: An answer such as tres meses gives a duration; enero would be a starting point.

sentence: Ana, ¿hace cuánto devolviste el libro? Ya no está en tu casa.
grammar: Hace cuánto asks how much time has passed since the completed return. Devolviste places the event in the past.
note: The question asks when the return happened, rather than how long a situation has continued.

sentence: Ana, ¿cuánto tiempo hace que vives en esta casa?
grammar: Cuánto tiempo asks for the time quantity in cuánto tiempo hace que. Present vives identifies a residence that continues now.
note: Cuánto modifies masculine singular tiempo and carries an interrogative accent.

sentence: Llevo dos años aquí y todavía vivo con mi hermana.
grammar: Llevar with a time quantity and location expresses elapsed presence continuing now. Aquí supplies the location; no gerund is needed.
note: This temporal sense differs from carrying an object or wearing clothing.

sentence: Hoy cumplo cinco años en esta escuela; todavía trabajo aquí.
grammar: Cumplir with a time quantity can mark an anniversary in employment. Cinco años measures service at the school rather than the speaker's age.
note: The speaker reaches the five-year milestone today and continues working there.

sentence: La reunión duró dos horas; empezó a las cuatro y terminó a las seis.
grammar: Durar states an event's overall length. Preterite duró presents the meeting as finished, with its start and end given.
note: Two hours is the meeting's duration rather than time since it happened.

sentence: Hoy tardé media hora en preparar la cena; ya está lista.
grammar: Tardar states the time needed to accomplish an action, introduced by en with an infinitive. Preterite tardé presents today's preparation as completed.
note: The ready dinner supplies a completed result.

sentence: Llegué a la clínica a las ocho; ya pasaron dos horas y sigo aquí.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present continuative state verb
grammar: Seguir with a location expresses continued presence. Sigo aquí says that the speaker remains at the clinic after two hours; there is no gerund.
register: Everyday update about a prolonged stay.
note: This use continues a location state rather than describing following a route.

sentence: Ayer esperé un rato en la entrada; después llegó mi hermana.
grammar: Un rato measures an unspecified stretch of waiting.
note: The wait lasts a while; the phrase does not specify an exact number of minutes.

sentence: Ayer dejé de escribir un momento y luego terminé el mensaje.
grammar: Un momento measures the brief interruption between writing and finishing the message.
register: Everyday account of a completed task.
note: This is an actual brief interval in a past account. The speaker is not asking someone to wait.

sentence: El teléfono sonó un instante y dejó de sonar.
grammar: Un instante measures how briefly the ringing lasted before it stopped.
note: Instante emphasizes a very short interval without giving an exact measurement.

sentence: Viví una temporada con mi tía, de junio a agosto; en septiembre volví a casa.
grammar: Una temporada describes the extended but temporary residence. The months and return home bound the stay.
note: Temporada here does not name a particular season of the year.

sentence: Durante una época de mi infancia, iba a casa de mis abuelos cada tarde.
grammar: Una época identifies a period characterized by a repeated childhood routine. Iba presents that routine in the imperfect.
note: The period is identified through a life stage and its routine, rather than an exact calendar date.

sentence: Viví una década con mis padres; ahora vivo con mi hermana.
grammar: Una década measures a completed ten-year period of residence. Ahora vivo contrasts it with the present household.
note: Década means a ten-year span; it need not coincide with a named calendar decade.

sentence: En mi cuento, la casa estuvo vacía durante un siglo; después llegó una familia.
grammar: Durante un siglo measures a finished hundred-year interval in the house's fictional history.
note: The sentence describes an invented story, with the family's arrival ending the empty period.

sentence: La renta del cuarto es de mil pesos por una quincena; puedo quedarme quince días.
grammar: Una quincena states the period covered by the room rental. Quince días makes its length explicit.
note: This arrangement covers fifteen days. The sentence does not define every rental or payment cycle.

sentence: Estudié música durante un semestre, de enero a junio, antes de volver al trabajo.
grammar: Un semestre names the six-month period spent studying. De enero a junio supplies the calendar span.
note: The sentence gives this study period's length; individual school calendars can organize teaching dates differently.

sentence: El curso de cocina dura un trimestre: empieza en abril y termina en junio.
grammar: Un trimestre gives the course's overall length. The named months identify the three-month interval.
note: Here the interval covers April, May and June.

sentence: Mi jornada de trabajo en la cocina empezó a las ocho y terminó a las cuatro.
grammar: Jornada de trabajo names the day's work period, bounded by its starting and finishing times.
note: The noun refers to the period of work in the kitchen, rather than a journey.

sentence: Tengo un plazo de tres días para entregar la tarea; empecé hoy.
grammar: Plazo names the allowed interval for completing and submitting the task. De tres días specifies its length.
note: The three days are available for the task; they are not three days already spent working.

sentence: El intervalo entre mi salida de casa a las siete y mi llegada al trabajo a las ocho fue de una hora.
grammar: Intervalo names the span between the departure and arrival. Entre links the two explicit endpoints.
note: The hour runs from leaving home at seven to reaching work at eight.

sentence: Estuve dos horas en la oficina; en ese lapso contesté diez correos.
grammar: Ese lapso refers back to the completed two-hour period at the office.
register: Neutral to slightly written work account.
note: The span is a period during which the replies were written, not an exact moment.

sentence: Mi antigüedad en la empresa es de cinco años; todavía trabajo aquí.
grammar: Antigüedad measures how long the speaker has worked for the company.
note: The five years measure employment service, rather than the age of an old object.

sentence: Mi permanencia en la biblioteca fue de ocho a doce; después volví a casa.
meaning: time spent remaining at a place
grammar: Permanencia names the time the speaker remained at the library. De ocho a doce supplies both endpoints.
note: This noun can describe a temporary presence; it does not imply staying forever.

sentence: Ayer la espera del camión duró cuarenta minutos; llegó a las ocho.
grammar: La espera is a noun naming the waiting period. Duró states its length, and the bus's arrival ends it.
note: The article la marks the noun. This is not the verb form espera.

sentence: Mi estancia en casa de mi hermana duró una semana; después volví a mi casa.
grammar: Estancia names the period spent staying at the sister's home. The return to the speaker's own home makes the temporary stay clear.
note: Here estancia means a stay, rather than a room in a house.

sentence: El trayecto de mi casa a la clínica duró veinte minutos; llegué a tiempo para mi cita.
grammar: Trayecto names the journey from the stated origin to the stated destination. Duró measures its travel time.
note: The twenty minutes measure travel to the clinic, not the appointment or an entire vacation.

sentence: Ayer el recorrido por el centro duró dos horas, con paradas en el mercado y en el parque.
grammar: Recorrido names a route followed as an activity. The stops form part of its two-hour duration.
register: Neutral account of a local outing.
note: The market and park are stops along the tour, rather than merely its starting and finishing points.

sentence: Mi consulta con la médica duró veinte minutos; hablamos del dolor de espalda.
grammar: Consulta names the medical encounter itself, whose length is measured by duró veinte minutos.
note: The sentence describes time spent with a doctor and gives no medical advice.

sentence: Ana es enfermera; ayer su guardia en el hospital duró ocho horas, de las dos de la tarde a las diez de la noche.
grammar: Guardia names Ana's period on duty. The eight-hour interval runs from two in the afternoon to ten at night.
note: The word names the duty period here, rather than a person employed as a guard.

sentence: Estudié dos horas; el descanso duró quince minutos y después volví a estudiar.
grammar: Descanso names the rest interval between two periods of studying.
note: The speaker resumes studying after fifteen minutes, so this is a break within the activity.

sentence: Hicimos una pausa de diez minutos y después seguimos estudiando.
grammar: Hacer una pausa means to interrupt an activity temporarily. Seguimos estudiando makes the resumption explicit.
note: A pausa does not by itself say whether the interruption was used for rest.

sentence: Ana viajó del lunes al viernes; durante su ausencia cuidé a su perro.
grammar: Su ausencia refers to the period when Ana was away traveling, from Monday to Friday.
note: Both su forms refer to Ana: the absence is hers and the dog is hers.

sentence: El camión tenía que salir a las ocho, pero salió a las ocho y media; la demora fue de treinta minutos.
grammar: Demora names the extra time beyond the expected eight o'clock departure. The actual departure was at eight thirty.
note: The thirty minutes measure lateness, rather than the journey's duration.

sentence: La maestra dio una prórroga: la tarea era para el lunes y ahora es para el miércoles.
grammar: Prórroga names additional time granted for a task. The deadline moves from Monday to Wednesday.
note: The teacher grants the extension; this is not merely a late submission.

sentence: La vigencia de mi pase es del primero al treinta de junio; puedo entrar al museo durante esos días.
grammar: Vigencia names the period during which the pass permits entry. The beginning and end are explicitly dated.
note: The stated dates belong to this particular pass.

sentence: El vencimiento de mi pase es el treinta de junio; el primero de julio ya no puedo entrar con él.
grammar: Vencimiento names the endpoint of the pass's validity. Entry with that pass is unavailable the following day.
note: Vigencia names the valid period; vencimiento identifies its end.

sentence: Ayer esperé un segundo antes de contestar la llamada.
grammar: Un segundo measures the very short wait before answering.
register: Everyday account of a phone call.
note: A segundo is a unit shorter than a minute. Here it does not mean second in an ordered sequence.

sentence: Esperé media hora en la clínica; después la médica me llamó.
grammar: Media agrees with feminine hora. The phrase measures the completed wait before the doctor called the speaker.
note: Media hora is a duration. Y media after a clock hour means half past.

sentence: La película dura hora y media; empieza a las siete y después vamos a cenar a las nueve.
grammar: Hora y media gives the film's duration. The seven o'clock start leaves time before the planned nine o'clock dinner.
note: The phrase measures a length of time, rather than naming a clock time.

sentence: Ayer cuidé a mi papá todo el día, desde la mañana hasta la noche.
grammar: Todo el día extends the caregiving across the day's span. Desde la mañana hasta la noche makes that span explicit.
note: The phrase describes an all-day responsibility, rather than a particular hour.

sentence: He llamado a mi hermana tres veces a lo largo de este mes; seguimos organizando su visita.
grammar: A lo largo de distributes the three calls across the month. The perfect presents accumulated contact in a period extending to now.
note: The calls occur on separate occasions; the phrase does not mean continuous calling.

sentence: Ayer trabajé dos horas sin parar; después descansé quince minutos.
grammar: Sin parar describes the two hours of work as continuous. The rest occurs afterward.
note: The uninterrupted work period contrasts with the explicitly stated later rest.

sentence: Ayer leí el cuento de corrido, sin pausas, y después cerré el libro.
grammar: De corrido describes reading the story continuously. Sin pausas makes the absence of interruptions explicit.
note: The expression concerns continuity; it does not specify reading speed.

sentence: En mi curso de cocina, al principio necesitaba ayuda; ahora preparo la cena solo.
grammar: Al principio locates the need for help in the initial part of the cooking course. Ahora introduces the later situation.
note: Unlike desde el principio, this phrase identifies the initial phase without saying that the situation continued throughout.

sentence: Empecé este trabajo a mediados de mayo; ahora, en junio, ya conozco a todos mis compañeros.
grammar: A mediados de places the start of the job in the middle part of May. The following month supplies a later reference point.
note: The phrase does not require an exact date such as the fifteenth.

sentence: Volví a casa a finales de agosto; en septiembre empecé las clases.
grammar: A finales de locates the return home in the final part of August. The start of classes follows in September.
note: The phrase identifies a portion near the month's end, rather than the whole month's duration or necessarily its final day.

sentence: Llegué a esta ciudad a principios de enero; ahora, en marzo, ya conozco las calles del centro.
grammar: A principios de locates the arrival in the early part of January. Ahora, en marzo contrasts that onset with the current situation.
register: Neutral conversation about settling into a city.
note: The expression gives an approximate early portion of the month, without specifying an exact arrival date.

sentence: Luis es mi amigo desde siempre; todavía nos vemos los domingos.
meaning: for as long as I can remember
grammar: Desde siempre presents the friendship as extending back throughout the speaker's remembered life. Todavía nos vemos makes continued contact explicit.
note: The expression gives no exact starting date.

sentence: Trabajo en esta escuela desde enero hasta hoy; sigo aquí como maestro.
grammar: Hasta hoy brings the employment interval to today. Sigo aquí como maestro explicitly confirms that the employment is still current.
note: The phrase alone does not guarantee continuation beyond today; the following clause supplies current status.

sentence: En este curso he leído tres libros hasta ahora; sigo estudiando.
grammar: Hasta ahora sets the present as the endpoint for the accumulated reading. Sigo estudiando keeps the course activity open.
note: Ahora refers to the present moment; entonces would refer back to another established time.

sentence: Ayer viajé solo por primera vez; antes siempre viajaba con mi mamá.
grammar: Por primera vez identifies yesterday's solo trip as the first such occurrence. The imperfect viajaba describes the earlier repeated arrangement.
note: The first occurrence concerns traveling alone, not necessarily the speaker's first trip.

sentence: Mi papá ha venido varias veces últimamente; seguimos comiendo juntos los domingos.
grammar: Últimamente names a recent period extending to now. Varias veces makes the visits repeated, and the following clause confirms continuing shared meals.
note: The adverb supplies a recent time frame; it does not impose one tense in every context.

sentence: En los últimos tres días he llamado varias veces a la clínica; todavía no tengo cita.
grammar: Últimos agrees with masculine plural días. Los últimos tres días identifies the recent three-day interval reaching the present.
note: The calls are repeated and an appointment is still pending.

sentence: Voy a trabajar en casa a partir de mañana; hoy todavía voy a la oficina.
grammar: A partir de introduces tomorrow as the prospective start of working at home. Today's office trip precedes that change.
note: The new arrangement has not started yet; desde commonly introduces an already established starting point in ongoing accounts.

sentence: Ayer lavé los platos antes de salir de casa.
grammar: Antes de places washing the dishes earlier than leaving home. The infinitive salir has the same understood actor as lavé.
note: Both actions belong to the speaker's account of yesterday.

sentence: Ayer fui a la farmacia después de mi consulta con la médica.
grammar: Después de places the pharmacy visit later than the medical consultation named by the following noun phrase.
note: The phrase orders events in time; it does not describe a spatial route.

sentence: Voy a visitar a mi hermana dentro de dos días.
grammar: Dentro de measures the interval from now to the planned visit. Voy a visitar expresses the speaker's plan.
note: Dentro de dos días points forward; hace dos días places an event two days before now.

sentence: Ayer llegué a casa a las seis y al cabo de una hora terminé la tarea.
grammar: Al cabo de measures an hour from yesterday's six o'clock arrival to the completion of the homework.
register: Neutral account of a completed task.
note: The reference point is the stated past arrival, rather than the present moment.

sentence: Mi hermana llegó el lunes y al día siguiente fuimos al museo.
grammar: Al día siguiente refers to the day after the sister's Monday arrival. Fuimos includes the speaker and the sister.
note: The expression is relative to the past arrival; mañana would mean tomorrow from the current speaking point.

sentence: Mi cita con la médica fue el martes; la víspera preparé mis papeles.
part_of_speech: feminine singular temporal noun phrase used adverbially
grammar: La víspera identifies the day before the Tuesday appointment. Preparé describes getting the documents ready on that earlier day.
note: The reference event is the appointment, so the preparation took place on Monday.

sentence: Desde enero visito a mi abuela de vez en cuando; no tenemos un día fijo.
grammar: De vez en cuando describes occasional separate visits within the period beginning in January and continuing now.
note: The expression gives occasional frequency, rather than the length of one visit.

sentence: Desde marzo limpio el baño cada dos días, un día sí y un día no.
grammar: Cada dos días gives the recurring interval between cleaning occasions. Un día sí y un día no makes the alternating pattern explicit.
note: The phrase does not mean that each cleaning takes two days.

sentence: Voy a la biblioteca cada tercer día; esta semana voy el lunes, el miércoles y el viernes.
grammar: Cada tercer día idiomatically expresses alternate-day repetition. Inclusive counting treats a visit day as day one, the intervening day as day two, and the next visit day as day three.
register: Everyday Mexican conversation about a routine.
note: The Monday, Wednesday, and Friday visits illustrate the alternation. The expression does not mean three full days between visits.

sentence: Desde mayo leo el periódico a diario, también los domingos.
grammar: A diario expresses daily occurrence within the continuing period beginning in May. Leo supplies the already familiar habitual present.
note: The sentence explicitly includes Sundays in the reading routine.

sentence: Mi hermana pidió ayuda y fui de inmediato a su casa.
grammar: De inmediato presents the trip as a response without practical delay after the sister's request for help.
note: The expression signals promptness without stating an exact number of seconds or minutes.

sentence: Luis me pidió ayuda con la tarea y le respondí: «Voy enseguida».
grammar: Enseguida promises prompt movement in the speaker's direct response to Luis's request.
note: Voy enseguida means the speaker will go right away or very soon.

sentence: Estoy limpiando la casa y todavía falta la cocina; tengo para rato.
grammar: In tengo para rato, the phrase indicates that the current cleaning will occupy the speaker for a considerable further period.
note: The unfinished kitchen gives a concrete reason to expect continued work.

sentence: La enfermera que cuida a mi papá se llama Ana.
grammar: Que refers to la enfermera and is the subject of cuida. The relative information identifies which nurse is named Ana.
note: This unaccented que modifies a person noun; it does not ask a question.

sentence: El camión que pasa por mi calle va al hospital.
grammar: Que refers to el camión and is the subject of pasa. The street is part of the bus's route, rather than the antecedent of que.
note: Que can identify a thing as well as a person.

sentence: El libro que Ana lee es de mi hermano.
part_of_speech: relative pronoun functioning as direct object
grammar: Que represents el libro as the direct object of lee. Ana is the separately expressed subject doing the reading.
note: Spanish keeps the relative pronoun here even when English can omit that.

sentence: La médica que mi papá conoce trabaja en este hospital.
part_of_speech: relative pronoun functioning as direct object
grammar: Que represents la médica as the person known. Mi papá is the subject of conoce; the doctor is the subject of trabaja.
register: Neutral conversation about a personal acquaintance.
note: The relative pronoun que can refer to a person as direct object.

sentence: Los niños que esperan en la entrada van a mi clase.
grammar: Que is the subject of esperan and refers to plural los niños. The relative verb therefore takes plural -an agreement.
note: The children perform the waiting action. The relative verb agrees with those children, while que itself remains unchanged.

sentence: Los papeles que yo necesito están en mi bolsa.
grammar: Necesito agrees with explicit subject yo. Que represents plural los papeles as the relative verb's direct object, so the papers do not trigger plural agreement in necesito.
note: The main verb están is plural because the documents are its subject. Inside the relative clause, yo controls necesito.

sentence: La camisa que está limpia es mía; el pantalón limpio es de Luis.
grammar: Inside que está limpia, que represents feminine singular camisa. The predicate adjective therefore takes feminine singular limpia. The separate adjective limpio agrees with masculine pantalón.
note: The relative describes the shirt, so its predicate adjective follows camisa's gender even though the immediately preceding subject word is invariant que.

sentence: La compañera con quien trabajo se llama Julia.
part_of_speech: preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: Con belongs to trabajar con alguien. Quien refers to the singular person la compañera, identifying Julia through their working relationship.
note: With an explicit antecedent in this identifying construction, quien follows a preposition.

sentence: Los compañeros con quienes estudio viven cerca de mi casa.
part_of_speech: preposition and plural personal relative pronoun
grammar: Quienes is plural because its antecedent is los compañeros. Con marks the people sharing the speaker's study activity.
note: The number of quienes follows the people referred to, even though estudio has the singular subject I.

sentence: La vecina a quien le di las llaves vive arriba.
part_of_speech: recipient preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: A quien identifies la vecina as the recipient of las llaves. Le repeats that singular recipient, and di identifies the speaker as giver.
note: The keys are the direct object; the neighbor receives them.

sentence: Los alumnos a quienes les presto estos libros tienen examen mañana.
part_of_speech: recipient preposition and plural personal relative pronoun
grammar: A quienes refers to plural los alumnos as the recipients of the loan. Les marks the same recipients; estos libros names the direct objects.
note: Presto is singular because the speaker lends the books; quienes is plural because several students receive them.

sentence: Ana, el médico de quien te hablé ayer trabaja en esta clínica.
part_of_speech: topic preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: De comes from hablar de alguien and marks the doctor as the topic of yesterday's conversation. Te refers to the listener Ana.
note: De quien means about whom here, rather than expressing ownership.

sentence: La niña para quien preparo esta sopa es mi hija.
part_of_speech: beneficiary preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: Para quien identifies la niña as the intended beneficiary of preparing the soup. The speaker is the understood subject of preparo.
note: The soup is being prepared for the daughter; she is not the person doing the preparation.

sentence: Luis está enfermo; es el compañero por quien voy a cubrir el turno de hoy.
part_of_speech: substitution preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: Por quien identifies Luis as the person the speaker will substitute for. Cubrir el turno makes the replacement work explicit.
note: Por marks substitution here; para quien would present someone as an intended beneficiary.

sentence: Ana, quien es enfermera, vive cerca de mi casa.
part_of_speech: singular personal relative pronoun in an explanatory clause
grammar: Quien adds information about the already named Ana. The commas mark the information as explanatory rather than necessary to identify her.
note: Bare quien is possible in this explanatory use; the earlier identifying examples used a preposition.

sentence: Ana y Luis, quienes viven cerca de mi casa, vienen a cenar los viernes.
part_of_speech: plural personal relative pronoun in an explanatory clause
grammar: Quienes adds information about the already named pair Ana y Luis. Both quienes and viven are plural; commas enclose the explanatory information.
note: Quienes refers to both people, while the main clause describes their Friday dinner visits.

sentence: La casa donde vivo está cerca de la escuela.
grammar: Donde refers to the explicit place la casa and introduces the information that the speaker lives there.
note: Relative donde has no written accent. Interrogative dónde asks a location question.

sentence: La biblioteca en donde estudio abre a las ocho.
grammar: En donde introduces the library as the location of the speaker's studying. In this sentence, donde without en also expresses that location.
note: En is optional here; it does not create a different location meaning.

sentence: La clínica adonde voy en camión está lejos de mi casa.
grammar: Adonde refers to la clínica as the destination of voy. En camión specifies the transport used to reach it.
note: This relative has no written accent. A donde is also a valid spelling for the destination relative.

sentence: La terminal de donde sale el camión está cerca de mi casa.
part_of_speech: source preposition and locative relative adverb
grammar: De donde refers to la terminal as the source of the bus's departure. De supplies the origin relation required by salir de un lugar.
note: De donde identifies the departure point; adonde identifies a destination.

sentence: La ventana desde donde veo la entrada está abierta.
part_of_speech: viewpoint preposition and locative relative adverb
grammar: Desde donde identifies la ventana as the viewpoint from which the speaker sees the entrance.
note: The relative describes a viewing position rather than a departure.

sentence: El pasillo por donde llevo las sillas está vacío.
part_of_speech: route preposition and locative relative adverb
grammar: Por donde identifies el pasillo as the route used to carry the chairs.
note: Llevo makes movement through the corridor explicit.

sentence: La esquina hasta donde vamos a caminar está al lado de la farmacia.
part_of_speech: spatial endpoint preposition and locative relative adverb
grammar: Hasta donde identifies la esquina as the endpoint of the planned walk.
note: The endpoint is a physical place.

sentence: El día en que empezó el curso conocí a Ana.
grammar: En que refers to el día as the time when the course began. The main clause places the speaker's first meeting with Ana on that same day.
note: A day can be the antecedent of a relative clause; en introduces the temporal relationship here.

sentence: La vecina en quien confío cuida a mi hija.
part_of_speech: governed preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: En belongs to confiar en alguien, meaning to trust someone. Quien refers to la vecina; the speaker is the understood subject of confío, and the neighbor is the subject of cuida.
register: Neutral written or careful spoken description.
note: Spanish keeps en from confiar en even though English usually says the neighbor whom I trust.

sentence: El parque hacia donde caminamos ahora está al lado de la escuela.
part_of_speech: direction preposition and locative relative adverb
grammar: Hacia donde identifies el parque as the direction of the group's current walk. Ahora makes the current movement explicit.
note: Hacia marks direction toward the park; it does not assert that the walkers reach it.

sentence: Tengo dos libros de cocina; uso el que tiene fotos.
part_of_speech: masculine singular article and relative pronoun with an omitted noun
grammar: El que stands for el libro que. Masculine singular el agrees with the omitted libro.
note: The relative identifies one of the two cookbooks.

sentence: Hay dos camisas limpias; la que está en la silla es mía.
part_of_speech: feminine singular article and relative pronoun with an omitted noun
grammar: La que stands for la camisa que. Its feminine gender follows the omitted garment noun.
note: La identifies a shirt here; it does not refer to a female person.

sentence: De estos cinco vasos, uso los que están limpios.
part_of_speech: masculine plural article and relative pronoun with an omitted noun
grammar: Los que stands for los vasos que and selects a subset of the five glasses. Están is plural because the glasses are its subject.
note: The visible set contains five glasses; the speaker uses its clean members.

sentence: Tengo cuatro camisas; las que están en esta bolsa son para el trabajo.
part_of_speech: feminine plural article and relative pronoun with an omitted noun
grammar: Las que stands for las camisas que. The selected shirts are the plural subject of both están and son.
note: Feminine plural las follows camisas, the omitted noun.

sentence: Entiendo lo que dice este aviso: la entrada está cerrada.
part_of_speech: neuter article and relative pronoun referring to content
grammar: Lo que introduces the content of the notice. It does not replace a masculine or feminine noun.
note: The words after the colon state the notice's content.

sentence: Ya tengo todo lo que necesito para la clase: el libro y un lápiz.
part_of_speech: totalizing quantifier with a neuter relative sequence
grammar: Todo makes the relative sequence refer to the complete set of needed materials. Necesito para la clase remains outside the blank.
note: The book and pencil make the complete set concrete.

sentence: Tengo algo que sirve para abrir esta caja: una llave pequeña.
grammar: Algo introduces an existing but initially unnamed item. The indicative sirve describes what that item does.
note: The speaker has the item and identifies it after the colon.

sentence: La escuela a la que va mi hija está cerca de casa.
part_of_speech: destination preposition with a feminine singular article and relative pronoun
grammar: A comes from ir a la escuela. La agrees with the feminine antecedent escuela, and mi hija is the subject of va.
note: The preposition preserves the destination relationship inside the relative.

sentence: El café en el que trabajo abre a las siete.
part_of_speech: locative preposition with a masculine singular article and relative pronoun
grammar: En el que refers to el café as the location of the speaker's work. El agrees with café.
note: Donde can also express this location: el café donde trabajo.

sentence: La cuchara con la que mezclo la sopa está limpia.
part_of_speech: instrument preposition with a feminine singular article and relative pronoun
grammar: Con introduces the instrument used to mix the soup. La agrees with cuchara.
note: The spoon is the tool; the speaker performs the mixing.

sentence: El libro del que hablamos trata de cocina.
part_of_speech: contracted topic preposition and masculine article with a relative pronoun
grammar: Del contracts de and el. De belongs to hablar de algo, and el agrees with libro.
note: The relative marks the topic of discussion rather than an owner.

sentence: El niño para el que preparo estos tacos no come queso.
part_of_speech: beneficiary preposition with a masculine singular article and relative pronoun
grammar: Para el que identifies el niño as the intended beneficiary of preparing the tacos. El agrees with niño.
note: The boy will receive the food; the speaker prepares it.

sentence: La calle por la que camino a la escuela está cerca de mi casa.
part_of_speech: route preposition with a feminine singular article and relative pronoun
grammar: Por marks the street used as a walking route. La agrees with the antecedent calle.
note: Camino a la escuela makes movement along the street explicit.

sentence: Los vecinos a los que les doy pan viven al lado de mi casa.
part_of_speech: recipient preposition with a masculine plural article and relative pronoun
grammar: A los que identifies los vecinos as recipients. Les marks the same plural recipients, while pan is the transferred object.
note: Doy agrees with the speaker; los refers to the neighbors receiving the bread.

sentence: La mesa de segunda mano cuesta menos que la nueva, pero ambas están en buen estado.
grammar: De segunda mano modifies mesa and describes its previous ownership.
note: A preowned item can still be in good condition.

sentence: Hace frío; voy a usar una camisa de manga larga para cubrir los brazos.
grammar: De manga larga modifies camisa and describes the length of its sleeves.
note: Manga means sleeve in this clothing expression.

sentence: Hace calor en la cocina; cambio mi camisa de manga larga por una de manga corta.
grammar: De manga corta modifies the omitted camisa after una. Cambiar una cosa por otra expresses replacing one item with another.
note: The alternative has shorter sleeves, appropriate to the speaker's hot kitchen.

sentence: Ana lleva una blusa sin mangas debajo de la chamarra.
grammar: Sin mangas modifies blusa. Sin excludes sleeves from the garment's design.
note: The blouse is worn underneath a jacket.

sentence: Mi camisa de rayas está en la silla; la blanca es de Ana.
grammar: De rayas modifies camisa and identifies its pattern.
note: Rayas are stripes in this clothing description.

sentence: La camisa de cuadros es para el trabajo; la de rayas es para salir.
grammar: De cuadros describes a pattern of squares or crossing lines on the shirt.
note: The checked pattern differs from the stripes on the other shirt.

sentence: Para la foto del trabajo, necesito una camisa lisa, sin rayas ni cuadros.
grammar: Lisa agrees with feminine camisa and describes the absence of a pattern.
note: Sin rayas ni cuadros establishes the clothing-pattern sense rather than smooth texture.

sentence: La falda estampada tiene flores azules; la falda lisa es negra.
grammar: Estampada agrees with feminine falda and describes its printed design.
note: The blue flowers supply the design; the other skirt is plain.

sentence: El sastre me hace un traje a la medida: mide mi cintura y mis brazos.
grammar: A la medida modifies traje and describes clothing made using the wearer's measurements.
note: Me identifies the speaker as the person for whom the tailor makes the suit.

sentence: El curso para adultos es por la noche; todos los alumnos tienen más de dieciocho años.
part_of_speech: adjectival prepositional phrase marking intended participants
grammar: Para adultos modifies curso and specifies the age category of its intended participants.
note: The phrase describes who the course serves rather than who owns it.

sentence: Mi hija de seis años lee un libro infantil con dibujos grandes.
grammar: Infantil modifies libro and identifies its intended child audience.
note: The adjective classifies the book; it does not criticize someone's behavior.

sentence: Somos cuatro; vamos a pedir una pizza familiar para compartir.
part_of_speech: singular descriptive adjective indicating a serving size
grammar: Familiar modifies pizza and describes a size intended for sharing.
note: Here familiar concerns serving size rather than something already known.

sentence: La lámpara portátil tiene una batería; la llevo de la casa al patio para leer.
grammar: Portátil modifies lámpara and describes equipment designed to be carried between places.
note: The speaker carries the lamp outside for reading; portability is more than small size.

sentence: Esta lámpara recargable usa una batería que puedo cargar muchas veces.
grammar: Recargable modifies lámpara and indicates that its battery can receive a new charge for further use.
note: The visible relative describes repeated charging of the battery.

sentence: En la fiesta hay vasos desechables; cada invitado usa uno una sola vez.
grammar: Desechables agrees with plural vasos and describes items intended for disposal after use.
note: Una sola vez makes the single-use purpose explicit.

sentence: Mi botella reutilizable sigue en buen estado; la lavo y la uso todos los días.
grammar: Reutilizable modifies botella and describes an item intended to be used again.
note: Washing and using the bottle daily makes the repeated use visible.

sentence: Doblo la silla plegable y la guardo detrás de la puerta.
grammar: Plegable modifies silla and describes a design that folds for storage or transport.
note: The speaker folds the chair before storing it behind the door.

sentence: Esta chamarra resistente al agua protege de la lluvia ligera, pero no de una lluvia fuerte.
part_of_speech: adjectival phrase with a prepositional complement
grammar: Resistente al agua modifies chamarra. Al contracts a and el before agua.
note: Water resistance describes limited protection; this jacket is described as suitable for light rain.

sentence: La bolsa a prueba de agua mantiene los papeles secos bajo el agua durante diez minutos, según su etiqueta.
grammar: A prueba de agua modifies bolsa and describes protection against water entering under the stated conditions.
register: Neutral description of a product label.
note: The label's ten-minute claim specifies this bag's protection; the phrase does not specify unlimited immersion.

sentence: La camisa en oferta cuesta cien pesos; su precio normal es de ciento cincuenta.
meaning: on sale; at a reduced price
grammar: En oferta modifies camisa and indicates a reduced selling price.
note: The sale price is one hundred pesos, compared with the ordinary price of one hundred fifty.

sentence: Para el desayuno, prefiero fruta de temporada: en este mes hay muchas naranjas.
grammar: De temporada modifies fruta and identifies food associated with its current growing or harvesting season.
note: Here the phrase describes seasonal fruit, rather than a length of time.

sentence: Compro queso local: Ana lo hace con leche de su granja aquí en el pueblo.
grammar: Local modifies queso and identifies its production in the surrounding area.
note: Ana makes the cheese here; local describes its origin rather than the location of a nearby shop.

sentence: Ana prepara queso artesanal a mano en un taller pequeño, no en una fábrica.
grammar: Artesanal modifies queso and describes its production using craft methods. The adjective has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.
note: Artesanal describes a production method; casero describes something made at home.

sentence: Quiero dos tortillas recién hechas para la cena; todavía están calientes.
part_of_speech: adjectival phrase containing an adverb and feminine plural participle
grammar: Recién modifies hechas; hechas agrees with tortillas. The phrase describes the result of recent preparation.
note: The tortillas have already been made and are still hot.

sentence: Quiero un café sin azúcar para tomar aquí, por favor.
grammar: Sin azúcar modifies café and excludes sugar from the requested drink.
note: Azúcar means sugar. This order specifies an ingredient preference.

sentence: En el menú hay una sopa baja en sal; esa es la que quiero para comer.
grammar: Baja agrees with feminine sopa. En sal specifies what the food contains in a low amount.
note: Low in salt does not mean salt-free.

sentence: Para la cena, preparo frijoles con poca grasa; uso solo una cucharadita de aceite.
grammar: Poca agrees with feminine grasa. The phrase describes the amount of fat used in preparing the beans.
note: Grasa means fat; aceite means oil.

sentence: Para el desayuno prefiero leche sin lactosa; me gusta su sabor.
grammar: Sin lactosa modifies leche and identifies the requested dairy product.
note: Lactosa is lactose, a sugar naturally present in milk.

sentence: Necesito un boleto de ida a Puebla; no voy a regresar en este viaje.
grammar: De ida modifies boleto and specifies a ticket for the outward journey only.
note: The requested ticket does not include a return segment.

sentence: Quiero un boleto de ida y vuelta de Puebla a Toluca: salgo el viernes y regreso el domingo.
grammar: De ida y vuelta modifies boleto and includes both the outward and return journeys.
note: The traveler leaves on Friday and returns on Sunday.

sentence: Prefiero el camión directo a Puebla porque no quiero cambiar de camión durante el viaje.
grammar: Directo agrees with camión and describes a service that reaches the destination without a transfer.
note: A direct service can have intermediate stops; the phrase does not promise the shortest route.

sentence: El vuelo con escala en Monterrey sale de la Ciudad de México y llega a Tijuana por la tarde.
grammar: Con escala modifies vuelo; en Monterrey identifies the intermediate stopping point.
note: The flight stops in Monterrey before reaching Tijuana. The phrase alone does not specify a change of aircraft.

sentence: Busco un café cercano a la escuela para esperar a mi hija.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective taking an a complement
grammar: Cercano modifies café; a la escuela supplies the reference point for its proximity.
note: Here café means a coffee shop.

sentence: La dentista tiene una cita disponible mañana a las nueve; puedo ir a esa hora.
grammar: Disponible modifies cita and identifies an appointment slot that can still be booked.
note: The adjective describes an available appointment rather than someone's general free time.

sentence: Ese asiento está ocupado; mi papá está sentado ahí.
grammar: Ocupado agrees with asiento and describes a seat currently being used.
note: Here ocupado means that a seat is taken, rather than that a person is busy.

sentence: La mesa reservada a nombre de Rosa es para cuatro personas; ella llega a las ocho.
grammar: Reservada agrees with mesa and describes a table held for a prior booking.
note: A nombre de Rosa identifies the name on the reservation.

sentence: El desayuno está incluido en los mil pesos de la habitación; ese es el precio total.
grammar: Incluido agrees with desayuno. En introduces the price that already covers the breakfast.
note: The stated total of one thousand pesos covers both the room and breakfast.

sentence: Ana, voy a terminar la tarea pendiente esta noche; todavía falta una pregunta.
grammar: Pendiente modifies tarea and identifies work still awaiting completion.
note: One unanswered question explains why the assignment is still pending.

sentence: Necesito una reparación urgente de la puerta: no cierra y tengo que salir en diez minutos.
grammar: Urgente modifies reparación and indicates that the task needs prompt attention.
note: The door will not close, and the speaker must leave shortly.

sentence: El desayuno opcional cuesta cien pesos más; puedo pagar solo la habitación.
grammar: Opcional modifies desayuno and describes a service the customer may choose or decline.
note: The speaker can pay for the room without adding breakfast.

sentence: Después de comer, voy a dar un paseo por el parque con mi hermana.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb in a leisure-walk collocation
grammar: Dar combines with un paseo to express taking a leisurely walk. Voy a governs the infinitive dar.
note: The walk is through the park with the speaker's sister.

sentence: Voy a dar una vuelta por el barrio con Luis; regresamos en diez minutos.
grammar: Dar una vuelta expresses a short outing or look around. Por el barrio identifies the area visited.
note: The planned return in ten minutes makes this a brief outing.

sentence: Voy a dar aviso a mi jefa del cambio de horario: hoy entramos a las diez.
grammar: Dar aviso a alguien de algo identifies the person notified with a and the news with de.
note: The speaker will notify their boss about the changed starting time.

sentence: Mi mamá me da permiso para ir al cine con mis amigos este sábado.
grammar: Dar permiso para with an infinitive authorizes an action. Me identifies the speaker as the person receiving permission.
note: The speaker's mother authorizes the cinema outing.

sentence: Mi teléfono da lata todos los días: el sonido falla durante las llamadas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present idiomatic verbal expression
grammar: Dar lata describes something or someone causing annoyance or practical trouble.
register: Informal mild complaint; natural in Mexican Spanish.
note: Lata is part of the expression here. The recurring problem is the phone's unreliable sound.

sentence: Para contestar el mensaje, tengo a la mano el número de la oficina.
grammar: Tener a la mano describes having a needed item nearby and readily available. El número is the available information.
register: Everyday practical communication; natural in Mexican Spanish.
note: The expression does not require holding the item in a hand.

sentence: Tengo que tener cuidado al bajar estas escaleras: están mojadas.
grammar: Tener cuidado expresses acting cautiously. Tengo que governs the infinitive expression.
note: The wet stairs provide the concrete reason for caution.

sentence: Tengo que tener paciencia con la espera en el banco; todavía hay cinco personas antes de mí.
grammar: Tener paciencia expresses tolerating a wait or difficulty calmly. Con introduces what requires patience.
note: Five people are still ahead of the speaker at the bank.

sentence: Necesito hacer fila en el banco para pagar el recibo de luz.
grammar: Hacer fila expresses joining or waiting in a queue. Necesito governs the infinitive expression.
note: Recibo de luz means electricity bill in this context.

sentence: Voy a hacer una llamada a mi hermana Rosa para confirmar la hora de la comida.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb in a telephone-call collocation
grammar: Hacer combines with una llamada to express making a telephone call. A mi hermana Rosa identifies the person called.
note: The purpose of the call is to confirm the mealtime.

sentence: Estos zapatos me hacen daño en los pies; están muy apretados.
grammar: Hacen agrees with plural zapatos. Me identifies the affected person, and en los pies identifies where the shoes hurt.
note: The speaker describes discomfort from tight shoes.

sentence: Hay que poner atención a la explicación de la maestra para usar bien el mapa.
grammar: Poner atención a directs mental attention toward the complement introduced by a.
note: Poner has a figurative sense here; no physical object is being placed.

sentence: Voy a poner una queja en recepción porque no hay agua en mi habitación.
grammar: Poner una queja expresses formally raising a complaint with the relevant service staff.
note: The complaint concerns the lack of water in the speaker's room.

sentence: Los papeles estaban mezclados; los puse en orden por fecha y ahora encuentro cada recibo.
grammar: Poner en orden expresses organizing things. Los refers to papeles, and por fecha describes the organizing criterion.
note: The papers were mixed together; after sorting them, the speaker can find each receipt.

sentence: Ayer, Ana y yo quedamos de vernos hoy a las seis en el café.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite verb with a governed preposition
grammar: Quedar de with an infinitive expresses making an arrangement. Vernos identifies a meeting between Ana and the speaker.
note: The arrangement was made yesterday; the meeting is today at six.

sentence: Prometí ayudar a mi vecina con la mudanza; quiero quedar bien con ella.
part_of_speech: infinitive verbal expression with a governed preposition
grammar: Quedar bien con alguien expresses maintaining someone's good opinion through one's behavior. Con introduces that person.
note: The speaker wants to keep their promise to help their neighbor move.

sentence: Los domingos me gusta pasar tiempo con mi abuela; cocinamos juntas.
grammar: Pasar tiempo con expresses spending time in someone's company. Me gusta takes the infinitive expression as its singular subject.
note: Juntas identifies the speaker and grandmother as a female pair cooking together.

sentence: En clase, la maestra va a pasar lista: lee los nombres y cada alumno dice «presente».
grammar: Pasar lista expresses checking who is present by calling names.
note: Presente is the student's response meaning that they are here.

sentence: Hoy el arroz me salió bien con tu receta: está suave y tiene buen sabor.
grammar: Salir with a result evaluation describes how something turns out. Bien gives the positive evaluation, and me identifies the person whose cooking produced the result.
note: The rice is soft and tastes good. The completed cooking event naturally takes the simple preterite here despite hoy.

sentence: El taxi al aeropuerto me salió caro: pagué quinientos pesos por un trayecto de veinte minutos.
grammar: Salir with a price evaluation expresses the resulting cost. Caro evaluates that cost, and me identifies who paid it.
note: The speaker evaluates a five-hundred-peso, twenty-minute taxi ride as expensive.

sentence: Hoy traigo puesta una camisa verde para trabajar en la oficina.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present verbal expression with feminine singular agreement
grammar: Traer puesto describes clothing being worn. Puesta agrees with the feminine singular garment camisa.
register: Everyday clothing description; natural in Mexican Spanish.
note: The shirt is on the speaker's body; the expression describes a clothing state.

sentence: La cita de las diez me viene bien porque entro a trabajar a las doce.
grammar: Venir bien expresses suitability or convenience. Me identifies the person whose schedule the appointment suits.
note: The appointment fits the speaker's schedule before work.

sentence: Llegué a la parada a las ocho y diez y perdí el camión de las ocho.
grammar: Perder a scheduled vehicle means failing to catch it. The stated arrival is later than the bus's departure time.
note: Here the speaker missed a bus through late arrival.

sentence: Necesito buscar trabajo porque la tienda donde trabajaba cerró.
grammar: Buscar trabajo expresses seeking employment. Trabajo normally has no article in this expression.
note: The speaker needs employment after their former workplace closed.

sentence: No había suficientes sillas para la reunión; encontré una solución: usamos también las del comedor.
grammar: Encontrar una solución expresses discovering a way to resolve a problem.
note: Using the dining-room chairs resolves the shortage for the meeting.

sentence: Espero buenas noticias sobre mi solicitud de trabajo; quiero empezar pronto.
grammar: Esperar with a favorable noun object can express hope for an outcome. Buenas noticias names that hoped-for outcome.
note: The speaker wants a favorable response to their job application.

sentence: Al salir de casa, dejé la llave en la mesa para mi hermana.
grammar: Dejar with an object and a location expresses leaving that item in the stated place.
note: The speaker leaves home while the key remains on the table for their sister.

sentence: Mi pedido de pan ya está listo; voy a recoger el pedido en la panadería.
grammar: Recoger expresses collecting something prepared or held for someone at a service location.
note: The bread order is ready at the bakery.

sentence: Voy a recoger a mi papá en mi carro a la salida del trabajo y llevarlo a casa.
grammar: Recoger a alguien expresses going to collect a person for a trip. Personal a introduces mi papá.
note: The speaker will collect their father by car and take him home.

sentence: El mensajero va a entregar el paquete a la señora Ruiz en su oficina.
grammar: Entregar identifies a transfer to a recipient. A la señora Ruiz names that recipient without specifying movement toward the speaker.
note: The parcel's recipient and delivery location are explicit.

sentence: Devolví la camisa a la tienda y me devolvieron el dinero de la compra.
grammar: Devolver el dinero expresses refunding a payment. Me identifies the customer who receives the money back.
note: The shop staff refund the speaker after the shirt is returned.

sentence: Esta camisa es demasiado pequeña; necesito cambiar la camisa por una de mi talla.
grammar: Cambiar una prenda por otra expresses exchanging one garment for another. Por introduces the replacement.
note: The speaker needs a replacement shirt in a suitable size.

sentence: Necesito cambiar este billete de cien pesos por dos de cincuenta para pagar el taxi.
grammar: Cambiar a banknote for smaller banknotes expresses changing money without changing its total value.
note: One hundred-peso banknote becomes two fifty-peso banknotes.

sentence: Antes de comprar, quiero probarme esta chamarra para ver si me queda bien.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular reflexive clitic
grammar: Probarme combines probar with reflexive me: the speaker tries the jacket on their own body. Quiero governs the infinitive.
note: The speaker wants to check the jacket's fit before buying.

sentence: Antes de servir la sopa, voy a probar una cucharadita para saber si necesita sal.
grammar: Probar food expresses tasting a sample to assess it. Una cucharadita limits the amount to a teaspoonful.
note: The speaker samples the soup to assess its salt.

sentence: Antes de comprar esta radio, quiero probar el aparato para saber si funciona.
grammar: Probar a device expresses testing its operation.
note: The speaker wants to check whether the radio works before purchase.

sentence: Comparé mis dos libros: me quedo con el pequeño y regalo el grande.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present pronominal verb with a governed preposition
grammar: Quedarse con an item expresses choosing to retain it. Con introduces the retained item.
note: The speaker chooses which of their two books to keep and gives the other away.

sentence: Voy a pedir prestado un lápiz a mi compañero; lo devuelvo después de clase.
grammar: Pedir prestado expresses requesting temporary use of an item. A mi compañero identifies the person asked.
note: The stated return after class makes the request a loan.

sentence: Para entender la tarea, necesito prestar atención a la explicación de la maestra.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb in an attention collocation
grammar: Prestar combines with atención to express paying attention. A introduces the focus of attention.
note: Prestar atención and poner atención can both describe directing attention to an explanation.

sentence: Ayer mi mamá me tomó la temperatura con un termómetro porque yo tenía calor.
grammar: Tomar la temperatura expresses measuring body temperature. Me identifies the person whose temperature was measured.
note: The sentence recounts a completed measurement by the speaker's mother.

sentence: Después de estudiar dos horas, voy a tomar un descanso de diez minutos.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb in a rest-break collocation
grammar: Tomar combines with un descanso to express taking a break from an activity.
note: The planned ten-minute break follows two hours of study.

sentence: Necesito sacar una cita con el dentista para el lunes; todavía no tengo ninguna.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb in an appointment collocation
grammar: Sacar una cita expresses obtaining or booking an appointment.
register: Everyday service planning; natural in Mexican Spanish.
note: The speaker is arranging a new appointment.

sentence: Hoy saqué dinero del cajero automático para pagar el taxi en efectivo.
grammar: Sacar dinero from a cash machine expresses withdrawing cash. Saqué uses qu before the preterite ending é.
note: The completed withdrawal takes the simple preterite naturally with hoy here.

sentence: Necesito sacar una copia de este documento en la papelería para la escuela.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb in a document-copy collocation
grammar: Sacar una copia expresses making a copy of a document. De introduces the document copied.
note: The speaker needs a copy for school.

sentence: Después de limpiar la cocina, voy a sacar la basura al contenedor de la calle.
grammar: Sacar la basura expresses taking household rubbish out. Al introduces its destination.
note: The rubbish goes from the home to the street container.

sentence: Antes del viaje, metí los zapatos en la bolsa para llevarlos a casa de mi hermana.
grammar: Meter an object en a space expresses moving it into that space. Metí is the regular first-person preterite.
note: The shoes move into the bag, contrasting with sacar for movement out.

sentence: Necesito guardar el recibo de esta camisa para una posible devolución.
grammar: Guardar here expresses retaining an item for possible later use.
note: The speaker keeps the receipt as a record for a possible return.

sentence: La empleada atiende a una clienta en la tienda y le muestra dos camisas.
grammar: Atender a una clienta expresses serving a customer. Atiende has the present e-to-ie stem change.
note: The employee serves the customer by showing her two shirts.

sentence: Estoy en una reunión y no puedo atender tu llamada ahora.
grammar: Atender una llamada expresses answering or dealing with a telephone call.
register: Neutral message to a familiar singular addressee.
note: The ongoing meeting explains why the speaker cannot answer the call now.

sentence: A mi hermana le avisé de un cambio de horario: hoy la clase empieza a las diez.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite verb with a governed preposition
grammar: Avisar a alguien de algo introduces the news with de. A mi hermana and le identify the person notified.
note: The notification concerns the class's changed starting time.

sentence: Ya tengo cita con el dentista el lunes; llamo para confirmar la hora acordada.
grammar: Confirmar an agreed appointment detail expresses verifying an existing arrangement.
note: The appointment already exists; the speaker calls to verify its agreed time.

sentence: Voy a cancelar mi cita del lunes porque ya no necesito la consulta.
grammar: Cancelar an appointment expresses removing it from the schedule entirely.
note: The speaker no longer needs the consultation and plans to cancel.

sentence: Hola, necesito reprogramar mi cita del martes al jueves porque trabajo el martes.
grammar: Reprogramar expresses assigning a new time or date to an existing arrangement. Del martes al jueves gives the old and new dates.
note: The speaker requests Thursday instead of Tuesday because of work.

sentence: Vamos a posponer la reunión de esta semana del lunes al viernes porque faltan dos compañeros.
grammar: Posponer expresses moving an event to a later time. Friday is later than Monday within the stated week.
note: The meeting will take place later in the same week.

sentence: Necesito adelantar mi cita de hoy de las doce del día a las nueve de la mañana.
grammar: Adelantar an appointment expresses moving it to an earlier time.
note: The requested change is from noon to nine in the morning on the same day.

sentence: Por la lluvia, la empresa va a retrasar la salida del camión de las ocho a las nueve de la mañana.
grammar: Retrasar a departure expresses moving it to a later time. The company is the actor making the change.
note: The bus departure changes from eight to nine in the morning because of rain.

sentence: De la escuela a casa hago un transbordo: bajo de un camión y subo a otro.
grammar: Un transbordo names a change from one vehicle to another during a journey. Hacer un transbordo expresses making that transfer.
note: The journey home requires getting off one bus and boarding another.

sentence: El tren sale del andén dos; espero ahí para subir.
grammar: Andén names the platform used to board or leave a train. Dos identifies its number.
note: The speaker waits at the numbered boarding place.

sentence: Nuestro viaje en camión termina en la terminal de autobuses; mi hermana nos espera dentro del edificio.
grammar: La terminal de autobuses names a bus transport facility. Here it is the journey's endpoint.
note: The sister waits inside the terminal building.

sentence: Para regresar de Puebla sin fecha fija, necesito un boleto abierto; voy a elegir la fecha más adelante.
meaning: ticket with no fixed travel date
grammar: Boleto abierto describes a travel ticket whose travel date remains to be chosen. Abierto modifies boleto.
note: The speaker wants to choose the return travel date later.

sentence: Necesito arreglar la silla: tiene una pata rota.
grammar: Arreglar a broken object means restoring its usable condition.
note: The broken chair leg selects the repair sense, rather than organizing things.

sentence: Voy a reparar la licuadora: el motor no gira.
grammar: Reparar takes the malfunctioning item as its direct object.
note: The stated defect is that the blender's motor does not turn.

sentence: El técnico va a componer el radio: no produce sonido.
grammar: Componer can take a device as its direct object to express restoring its operation.
register: Everyday repair conversation; natural in Mexican Spanish.
note: Here componer means repairing the radio, rather than composing music.

sentence: Mi teléfono no funciona; no puedo llamar a mi hermana.
grammar: Funcionar describes whether a device operates. The device is the grammatical subject.
register: Everyday account of a device problem.
note: This is a device's operation; trabajar describes working at a job.

sentence: El radio falla: a veces tiene sonido y a veces no.
grammar: Fallar describes unreliable operation with the device as subject.
note: The alternating presence and absence of sound makes the intermittent problem explicit.

sentence: El refrigerador se descompuso anoche; ahora la leche está caliente.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Descomponerse expresses a device breaking down. Se belongs to this pronominal verb; descompuso is its singular third-person preterite.
note: The refrigerator broke down last night; the warm milk shows the present problem.

sentence: Hay una fuga en el tubo: el agua sale por un agujero.
grammar: Una fuga names an unintended escape of water from a pipe in this context.
note: The water escaping through a hole establishes the water-leak sense.

sentence: Llueve y hay una gotera en el techo; el agua cae sobre la mesa.
grammar: Una gotera names a leak through a roof or ceiling that lets water drip inside.
note: Rain and water falling onto the table establish the roof-leak context.

sentence: El enchufe del cable del radio está roto; necesito cambiarlo.
grammar: El enchufe here identifies the plug on the radio's cable.
note: The cable identifies the plug being discussed, rather than the socket in a wall.

sentence: El contacto de la pared está detrás de la mesa; ahí conecto el radio.
grammar: Contacto names an electrical wall socket in this Mexican household context.
note: The socket is in the wall; enchufe in the preceding repair context identified the plug on the cable.

sentence: El foco de la lámpara ya no da luz; necesito uno nuevo.
grammar: El foco names the lamp's light bulb in ordinary Mexican household usage.
note: The lamp and its lack of light establish the bulb sense.

sentence: La llave del lavabo está abierta; por eso sale agua.
grammar: Llave can name the control through which water flows at a sink.
note: The sink and flowing water select faucet; llave also names a door key.

sentence: El reloj usa una pila pequeña; no necesita cable para funcionar.
grammar: Una pila names a small battery supplying power to the clock.
note: The power source is a battery, rather than a pile of objects.

sentence: Conecto el cargador a mi teléfono para cargar la batería.
grammar: El cargador names the device used to charge the phone's battery.
note: The phone and its battery establish the charger sense.

sentence: La pantalla de mi teléfono está rota; no puedo leer los mensajes.
grammar: La pantalla names the phone's display surface. Rota agrees with this feminine noun.
note: The broken screen prevents the speaker from reading messages.

sentence: La licuadora no funciona, pero tiene garantía: la tienda va a repararla sin costo.
grammar: Tener garantía describes a product having warranty coverage.
note: In this case, the shop will repair the faulty blender without charging for the repair.

sentence: Devolví el radio roto; el reembolso fue de cien pesos, todo el dinero que pagué.
grammar: El reembolso names the return of money paid for the product.
register: Neutral account of a product return.
note: This returns the purchase payment; cambio is money returned after overpaying at checkout.

sentence: Este pantalón es de mi talla, pero queda más holgado que el otro y me deja moverme bien.
grammar: Holgado describes a garment with room around the body and agrees with masculine pantalón.
note: The garment is the speaker's size; its roomier fit allows comfortable movement.

sentence: Compré esta camisa hoy, pero tiene una costura abierta bajo el brazo.
grammar: Una costura names the stitched join in the garment. Abierta describes a seam that has come apart.
note: The purchase is completed today, making the simple preterite natural in this Mexican context.

sentence: Lavé la camisa con jabón, pero todavía tiene una mancha de café.
grammar: Una mancha de café names a stain caused by coffee.
note: The coffee stain remains after washing.

sentence: El libro costaba veinte pesos; con el descuento, pagué quince.
grammar: Un descuento names a reduction from the original price.
note: The original price is twenty pesos and the amount paid is fifteen.

sentence: Doctora, tengo un síntoma nuevo: dolor de garganta.
grammar: Síntoma is masculine despite its final a: un síntoma nuevo.
note: The speaker reports a new sore throat.

sentence: Doctor, tengo mareo y siento que el cuarto gira.
grammar: Tener mareo expresses experiencing dizziness.
note: The speaker describes a sensation that the room is spinning.

sentence: Me dolía la espalda; después de descansar, sentí un poco de alivio, pero todavía me duele.
grammar: Sentir alivio expresses experiencing a reduction in discomfort. Un poco de specifies a limited amount.
note: Some back pain remains, so the relief is partial.

sentence: Mi hermana sigue enferma, pero hoy tiene menos dolor; es una pequeña mejoría.
grammar: Una mejoría names a favorable change in a person's condition.
note: The sister has less pain but is still ill.

sentence: Este zapato me causa una molestia en el pie porque me roza al caminar.
grammar: Una molestia names discomfort; me identifies the person affected.
note: The shoe rubbing against the foot supplies the concrete cause.

sentence: Hay una equivocación en mi pedido: pedí una sopa, pero recibí dos.
grammar: Una equivocación en identifies a mistake in an order or arrangement.
note: The speaker ordered one soup and received two.

sentence: Hubo una confusión con dos pedidos: Ana recibió la sopa de Luis y Luis recibió el café de Ana.
grammar: Una confusión con names a mix-up involving the stated items.
register: Neutral account of a service problem.
note: The two customers received each other's orders.

sentence: Hola, tengo un inconveniente con la cita del martes: trabajo a esa hora. ¿Puedo cambiarla al jueves?
grammar: Tener un inconveniente con introduces a practical difficulty concerning an arrangement.
note: The work schedule conflicts with the Tuesday appointment.

sentence: Pagué por dos cafés y recibí uno; voy a reclamar en la caja.
grammar: Reclamar here expresses raising a service complaint to seek correction.
note: The speaker paid for two coffees but received only one.

sentence: El técnico me va a cobrar cien pesos por reparar el radio.
grammar: Cobrar takes the amount charged; me identifies the customer, and por introduces the service.
note: The technician charges the customer; the customer pays, and the service costs a stated amount.

sentence: Necesitamos tres platos y tenemos cinco; van a sobrar dos.
grammar: Sobrar describes items exceeding what is needed. Dos refers to two plates and supplies the plural subject of van a sobrar.
note: Five plates are available and only three are needed.

sentence: Ayer tenía clase, pero tuve que faltar a clase: estaba enfermo y me quedé en casa.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with a governed preposition
grammar: Faltar a clase means being absent from class. A introduces the activity or obligation missed.
note: Class was scheduled, but the speaker stayed home because he was ill; this differs from faltar for missing objects.

sentence: Ana me ayudó con la tarea; quiero agradecerle su ayuda.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with an attached singular indirect-object pronoun
grammar: Agradecer takes the thing appreciated as direct object, su ayuda, and the person as indirect object. Attached le refers to Ana.
note: The speaker wants to thank Ana for her help with the homework.

sentence: Antes trabajaba en una tienda; actualmente trabajo en una escuela.
grammar: Actualmente places the employment situation in the present, contrasted with the former situation.
note: The selected ordinary sense is at present; English actually usually expresses a different idea.

sentence: El martes voy a asistir a la reunión; empieza a las nueve en la escuela.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with a governed preposition
grammar: Asistir a takes an event complement to express attending it.
note: Here the event complement selects attend. Asistir also has valid help or care senses in other contexts.

sentence: Hoy vamos a realizar una encuesta en clase: cada estudiante va a responder tres preguntas.
grammar: Realizar takes a task or activity as its direct object; here that activity is una encuesta.
register: Neutral to slightly formal school-project language.
note: Here realizar means carrying out an activity, rather than mentally realizing something.

sentence: Mi hermana está embarazada; su bebé va a nacer en mayo.
grammar: Embarazada agrees with hermana and follows estar to describe pregnancy.
note: The expected baby's birth establishes the everyday pregnancy sense.

sentence: Mi piel es sensible al jabón nuevo: después de lavarme, me pican las manos.
grammar: Sensible a introduces the stimulus producing sensitivity; al combines a and el. Sensible keeps its e ending with feminine piel.
note: The itching establishes physical sensitivity to soap. English sensible meaning practical has a different meaning.

sentence: Practicamos mucho y la presentación fue un éxito: todos entendieron la explicación.
grammar: Éxito is masculine: un éxito. Ser un éxito evaluates an event as having a favorable result.
register: Neutral positive school or work account.
note: Practice led to a presentation the audience understood. Éxito means success here; salida names an exit.
